Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. 45 Sector-wise Cooperatives A State’s three-tier rural cooperative credit structure consists of State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), and Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), which concentrate on agricultural and rural development. State cooperative banks are the apex institutions in this structure. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records the presence of 32 registered State Cooperative Banks in the country except for 5 States/UTs namely Haryana, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, Manipur, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. These cooperative banks offer a comprehensive range of services, from savings accounts to agricultural loans, actively supporting priority sectors and contributing to the well-being of local communities. With a clear mandate to promote financial inclusion and bolster essential sectors like agriculture and small-scale industries, cooperative banks remain instrumental in fostering economic growth and meeting the diverse needs of India’s population. 4.3 State Cooperative Bank (SCBs)

49 Sector-wise Cooperatives L ong-term rural credit cooperatives were established for providing funds for investment in agriculture – including land development, farm mechanisation and minor irrigation - rural industries and housing. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres (CSCs). Through the CSC framework, PACS can provide various e-governance and citizen-centric services. These can include services related to: * Banking * Insurance * Aadhaar enrolment or updation * Health services * Agricultural services * Government welfare schemes * Other permitted digital services The exact services available at a particular PACS may vary. --- ## Can PACS Become Multipurpose Cooperative Societies? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has prepared Model Bye-laws to help PACS diversify their activities and become multipurpose cooperative societies. The Model Bye-laws enable PACS to undertake more than 25 types of business activities across areas such as agriculture, dairy, fisheries, storage, retail and citizen services. Adoption and implementation are subject to the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act and State-level requirements. --- ## PACS Computerization The Government of India approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS in June 2022. The project aims to bring functional PACS onto an ERP-based common software system and connect them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks. The computerization initiative aims to: * Improve operational efficiency * Speed up loan disbursal * Reduce transaction costs * Improve accounting * Increase transparency * Improve coordination with DCCBs and StCBs --- ## PACS and Farmer Services PACS can act as a local point for farmers to access: * Agricultural credit * Agricultural inputs * Storage facilities * Marketing-related services * Government schemes * Digital citizen services * Other cooperative services The exact services available depend on the PACS and applicable schemes or permissions. --- ## Important Limitation for SIA PACS are governed by applicable cooperative laws and bye-laws. SIA should not assume that every PACS provides every possible service. For questions about: * Membership eligibility * Required documents * Loan amount * Interest rate * Repayment period * Specific loan products * Local PACS services * State-specific rules SIA should identify the relevant State/PACS and use the latest verified official information. --- ## Frequently Asked Questions / Retrieval Intents ### Definition * What is PACS? * What does PACS stand for? * What is a Primary Agricultural Credit Society? * What is a PACS society? * What is PACS in agriculture? * What is PACS in India? ### Functions * What does PACS do? * What services does PACS provide? * What are the functions of PACS? * What work does PACS do for farmers? * How does PACS help farmers? * What facilities are available through PACS? ### Membership * How can I become a PACS member? * How can I join PACS? * Who can become a PACS member? * What documents are needed to join PACS? * What are the requirements for PACS membership? * How do I apply for PACS membership? ### Credit and Loans * Can PACS give loans?

35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

The system connects warehouses and distributors to support availability of medicines and other products. ## Application / Access Route PACS interested in operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras should follow the applicable PMBJP and Ministry of Cooperation procedures. Current eligibility, approval, registration, drug licensing and operational requirements should be checked against the latest official PMBJP and Ministry of Cooperation guidelines. ## Eligibility / Conditions PACS can be allowed to open and operate Jan Aushadhi Kendras subject to the applicable Government procedures and conditions. Specific eligibility and approval requirements may change and should be verified from the latest official sources. ## Documents / Data Requirements Specific document requirements should be checked against the current PMBJP application, approval and drug licensing requirements. Do not assume a fixed document list without checking the latest official guidelines. ## Process Summary 1. Eligible PACS is identified / applies under the applicable process. 2. Initial approval is obtained through the relevant Government mechanism. 3. Required licensing and operational requirements are completed. 4. The PACS operates the Jan Aushadhi Kendra. 5. The Kendra supplies medicines and products under the PMBJP framework. 6. The PACS receives applicable margins and incentives subject to the scheme guidelines. ## FAQs / Query Intents ### What is a Jan Aushadhi Kendra by PACS? It is a Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra operated by a Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS). ### Can PACS open Jan Aushadhi Kendras? Yes. PACS can be allowed to open and operate Jan Aushadhi Kendras subject to the applicable Government procedures and conditions. ### Why are Jan Aushadhi Kendras being promoted through PACS? The initiative improves access to affordable medicines in rural areas and provides PACS with an additional economic activity. ### What are the benefits for PACS? PACS operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras can receive applicable trade margins and incentives under the PMBJP framework, subject to current guidelines. ### How many Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been opened through PACS? As of 30 June 2026, 846 Jan Aushadhi Kendras had been opened under PACS across the country. ### How many PACS have received initial approval? As of 30 June 2026, more than 4,250 PACS had received initial approval to open Jan Aushadhi Kendras. ### Is there a State-wise target for PACS Jan Aushadhi Kendras? No. As of the latest official information, there is no State/UT/District-wise target for opening new Jan Aushadhi Kendras through PACS. ### What is the target for Jan Aushadhi Kendras? The Government has set a target of opening 25,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras by March 2027. ### What is the trade margin for Jan Aushadhi Kendras? PACS operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras are eligible for the applicable benefits under PMBJP, including a 30% trade margin on MRP, subject to current guidelines. ### What medicines are covered by the stocking incentive? Since September 2024, stocking of 200 commonly used medicines has been incentivised: 100 top-selling medicines in the scheme product basket and 100 fast-selling

# World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector ## Scheme ID 09 ## Official Name World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector ## Type Cooperative sector / agricultural storage infrastructure initiative ## Ministry / Organisation Ministry of Cooperation ## Purpose The plan aims to create decentralized grain storage capacity at the Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) level by establishing godowns and other agricultural infrastructure. The initiative is intended to address the shortage of agricultural storage capacity and enable farmers to store their produce locally. ## Key Objective - Create decentralized grain storage capacity - Reduce post-harvest losses - Help farmers avoid distress sales - Improve local storage infrastructure - Strengthen PACS as multipurpose cooperative institutions ## PACS Role PACS are used as important points for developing decentralized grain storage infrastructure at the local level. PACS can also undertake related agricultural infrastructure and post-harvest activities. ## Major Components The plan provides for convergence with various existing schemes and programmes of different ministries to create agricultural infrastructure through PACS. Infrastructure may include: - Grain storage godowns - Custom Hiring Centres - Primary Processing Units - Other agricultural infrastructure as permitted under the programme ## Benefits to Farmers - Local storage facility closer to farms - Opportunity to store agricultural produce - Reduced dependence on distant storage facilities - Reduced possibility of distress sale immediately after harvest - Better post-harvest management ## Benefits to PACS - Diversification of PACS activities - Additional income-generating opportunities - Strengthening of PACS infrastructure - Greater role in agricultural supply-chain activities ## Implementation The plan is implemented through convergence of existing schemes of different ministries and departments. PACS are developed as decentralized storage and agricultural infrastructure points under the plan. ## Important Note The plan is implemented through convergence with existing government schemes. Specific financial assistance, infrastructure components, eligibility and implementation conditions depend on the applicable scheme and current government guidelines. ## Frequently Asked Questions / Intents ### What is the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan? It is a cooperative-sector initiative to create decentralized grain storage capacity at the PACS level. ### Why was the grain storage plan introduced? The plan aims to address the shortage of agricultural storage capacity, reduce post-harvest losses and help farmers avoid distress sales. ### What role do PACS play in the grain storage plan? PACS serve as important local-level institutions for developing decentralized grain storage and related agricultural infrastructure. ### Can grain storage facilities be established through PACS? Yes. The plan focuses on creating decentralized grain storage infrastructure at the PACS level. ### How does the plan benefit farmers? It provides local storage opportunities and can help farmers store produce instead of being forced to sell immediately after harvest. ### Does the plan only involve grain storage? No. The programme also supports convergence for related agricultural infrastructure such as Custom Hiring Centres and Primary Processing Units. ### Does the plan provide financial assistance? 103 Sector-wise Cooperatives 4.17 Agro Processing/Industry A gro processing could be defined as a set of techno-economic activities carried out for conservation and handling of agricultural produce and to make it usable as food, feed, fiber, fuel or industrial raw material. Hence, the scope of the agro-processing industry encompasses all operations from the stage of harvest till the material reaches the end users in the desired form, packaging, quantity, quality and price. In India, there are 22,341 Primary Agro Processing / Industrial Cooperatives, 7 State Level Federations, 11 District Level Federations and 1 Block/Taluka/Mandal Level Federation with total membership of 24,74,786, out of which 9,071 are functional, 9,239 are non-functional/ dormant and 4,031 are under liquidation process. Out of total, 11,561 cooperatives are registered in urban area and 10,780 are registered in rural area. Major Agro Processing/ Industrial States with highest number of registered cooperatives are Maharashtra (5,292), Uttar Pradesh (3,969) and Punjab (1,987). The cooperative societies in Maharashtra constitute the highest number of members i.e., 12,53,521 followed by Karnataka (4,53,612) and Gujarat (2,13,089). India being an agrarian economy, processing of agricultural produce is of vital importance and an important segment of the Indian economy in terms of contribution to GDP. It not only helps in value addition, but also in employment generation and exports of agri- produce. The key sub-segments of the Food Processing industry in India are Fruits & Vegetables, Poultry & Meat Processing, Fisheries, Food Retail, Dairy Industry, etc.

The remitted amount is added in a wallet of the Bank-Branch, CSC-VLE or Insurance Intermediary for onward remittance to the concerned Insurance Company implementing the scheme in a particular geographical area. These partner agencies (Bank Branches, CSC-VLEs & Insurance Intermediaries) can remit the premium amount multiple times to the concerned Insurance Companies before the cut-off-date. For each transaction, a Unique ID (UTR) is assigned using which reconciliation of payments and applications is done by the Insurance Companies. 39.4.3 Add-on Coverage of Crop Risk The State/UT has the option to notify Add-on perils cover with or without Basic Cover (Yield base cover). Selection of risk has been made available on portal as per the provisions available in the guidelines. In the notiﬁcation module, an option has been provided to the States/UTs to select the add-on coverage separately according to the crop and insurance unit along with the Basic Cover as per the notiﬁcation. Claim will be calculated on DigiClaim as per the add-on coverage opted for the crop and IU. 39.4.4 Land Record Integration Land record detail is one of the critical requirements under the PMFBY scheme for validation of insured area. Manual veriﬁcation of the land record data is a sheer challenge. Many State/UTs have digitized land record system, however their hierarchal system and practices are different. DA&FW has moved ahead to integrate the land record system of 10 major states with NCIP to validate the farmer's land parcel with land record system at the time of enrollment under the scheme. State/UTs shares the land record API subsequent to which customization of API consumption for integration of land records of the State(s) with NCIP is executed. The land record details of the farmers is required to be entered during enrolment process and rest of the land details viz. extent of land, ownership share and names of owners/shareholders are fetched through the State/UT land record portal. पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

य सहकारी सोसाइटी का मुख् य कायाकारी ऐसी ररजियों की सूचना, इसके उद्भुत होने के एक सप् ताह के भीतर प्राजधकरण को संसूजचत करेगा, िो अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार ररजियों को भरने की कारावाई करेगा । (2) अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार वैकजल्पक ररजियों में जनयुक्ट् त कोई ्‍ यजि अजधिेि अवजध तक ही बोडा का सिस्ट् य रहेगा, िब तक वह बोडा के सिस्ट् य जिसके स्ट् थान पर जनयुक्ट् त हुआ है, रहेगा । 19य. मतिान की गोपनीयता का अनुरिण - प्रत् येक अजधकारी, जलजपक, अजभकताा या अन्द् य ्‍ यजि िो दकसी जनवााचन में अजभलेखन या मतगणना से िुड़ा काया जनष् पािन कर रहा है, मतगणना की गोपनीयता अनुरजित करेगा और अनुरिण करने में मिि करेगा और दकसी अन्द् य ्‍ यजि को (जसवाए कुछ प्रयोिनों के जलए दकसी जवजध द्वारा या उसके अधीन प्राजधकृत) ऐसी गोपनीयता का उल् लंघन करने के जलए मतिान से संबंजधत कोई सूचना संप्रेजित नहीं करेगा ।” 5. मूल जनयमों में, जनयम 20 के स्ट् थान पर जनम् नजलजखत जनयम रखे िाएंगे, अथाातम: -

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

िाने वाले िस्ट् तावेि में हस्ट् तािर करने वाले सिस्ट् य का नाम, पिनाम, पता, सिस्ट् यता संख् या होगा और िो उसके सही होना सुजनजश्चत करेगा और कोई पत्राचार जिसमें मात्र प्राजधकृत हस्ट् तािरकताा जलखकर हस्ट् तािर कर दिया गया हो, को दकसी भी ििा स्ट् वीकारा नहीं िाएगा । 37च. अजधजनयम और उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन िस्ट् तावेिों का इलेक्ट् रॉजनक अनुरिण, पंिीकरण, और प्रमाणन - (1) प्रत् येक आवेिन, जववरणी, ररपोटा, लेखा जववरणी, रजिस्ट् टर, उपजवजधयां या अन्द् य कोई जववरण या िस्ट् तावेि जिसे अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन फाइल या पररचाजलत दकया िाना अपेजित है को केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा इलेक्ट् रॉजनक स्ट् वूपप में अनुरजित दकया िाएगा और अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा इसे रजिस्ट्रीकृत या प्रमाजणत, िो भी ििा हो, करने की आवश् यकता पड़ने पर, सूचना प्रौद्योजगकी अजधजनयम, 2000, आधार (जवत्तीय और अन्द् य सहाजयदकयों, प्रसुजवधाओं ओर सेवाओं का लजययत पररिान) अजधजनयम, 2016 और लागू अन्द् य जवजधयों और उनके अधीन बने उन जवजध, जवजधयों, दििाजनिेंिों, अजधसूचनाओं, या पररपत्रों के उपबंधों के अनुसार उसपर इलेक्ट् रॉजनक हस्ट् तािर लगाकर उसे रजिस्ट्रीकृत या प्रमाजणत दकया िाएगा । (2) उपजनयम (1) में जवजनर्िाि इलेक्ट् रॉजनक हस्ट् तािर के अजधप्रमाणन के जलए सूचना प्रौद्योजगकी अजधजनयम, 2000 और अन्द् य सुसंगत जवजधयों और उनके अधीन बने जनयमों, जवजनयमों, दििाजनिेंिों, अजधसूचनाओं, या पररपत्रों के अधीन स्ट् थाजपत प्रदक्रया लागू होगी। 37छ. धारा 120क के अधीन केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा िस्ट् तावेिों का िारीकरण और संप्रेिण - (1) केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार, अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन काया जनष् पािन या कत्ता्‍ यों का जनवाह्न या िजियों का प्रयोग या ऐसा कोई काया करेगा िो अजधजनयम द्वारा केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार को इलेक्ट् रॉजनक माध् यम से जनष् पादित या जनवाह्न या प्रयोग या करने के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, जनिेजित दकया गया हो

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

पर भी चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस नोरटस में जनम् नजलजखत सूचनाएं होंगी, अथाातम: (क) जनवााचन द्वारा भरी िाने वाली ररजियों की संख् या ; (ख) जनवााचन का िेत्र (उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट) जिसमें से सिस्ट् यों का जनवााचन दकया िाना है ; (ग) बोडा की सिस्ट् यता की पात्रता हेतु उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट अहाताएं, यदि कोई हैं ; (घ) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी का नाम, तारीख, स्ट् थान और समय जिस िौरान सिस्ट् यों द्वारा नामांकन कागज़ भरा िाएगा, वह तारीख िो जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख से न्द् यूनतम स्ट् पष् ट एक दिन पहले हो या यदि वह एक अवकाि का दिन है तो उससे पूवावती दिन िो सावािजनक अवकाि न हो । स्ट् पष् टीकरण- इस जनयम के प्रयोिन से िब् ि ‘सावािजनक अवकाि’ से ऐसा कोई दिन अजभप्रेत है िो परक्राम् य जलखत अजधजनयम, 1981 (1881 का 26) की धारा 25 के अधीन या ऐसा कोई दिन िो केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार द्वारा, िो भी ििा हो, केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार के कायाालयों के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, सावािजनक अवकाि के ूपप में अजधसूजचत की गई हो ; (ङ) वह तारीख और वह समय और स्ट् थान िब नामांकन कागिों की िांच की िाएगी; और (च) वह तारीख और समय तथा वह स्ट् थान और समय िब मतिान होगा । 19-स. सिस्ट् यों और प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची को तैयार करना - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा उस तारीख के अनुसार िो मतिान के जलए जनयत तारीख से तीस दिन पूवा मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों की सूची तैयार की िाएगी और सूची की प्रजतजलजपयों को सोसाइटी के कारबार के मूल स्ट् थान और इसकी सभी िाखाओं, यदि कोई हो, के नोरटस बोडा पर जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख के न्द् यूनतम पंरह दिन पूवा चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस सूची में जनम् नजलजखत जवजनर्िाष् ट होंगे - (क) सिस्ट् य का िाजखला संख् या और नाम, जपता या पजत का नाम, और व्यजिक की ििा में ऐसे सिस्ट् य का पता; और

पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

िाने वाले िस्ट् तावेि में हस्ट् तािर करने वाले सिस्ट् य का नाम, पिनाम, पता, सिस्ट् यता संख् या होगा और िो उसके सही होना सुजनजश्चत करेगा और कोई पत्राचार जिसमें मात्र प्राजधकृत हस्ट् तािरकताा जलखकर हस्ट् तािर कर दिया गया हो, को दकसी भी ििा स्ट् वीकारा नहीं िाएगा । 37च. अजधजनयम और उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन िस्ट् तावेिों का इलेक्ट् रॉजनक अनुरिण, पंिीकरण, और प्रमाणन - (1) प्रत् येक आवेिन, जववरणी, ररपोटा, लेखा जववरणी, रजिस्ट् टर, उपजवजधयां या अन्द् य कोई जववरण या िस्ट् तावेि जिसे अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन फाइल या पररचाजलत दकया िाना अपेजित है को केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा इलेक्ट् रॉजनक स्ट् वूपप में अनुरजित दकया िाएगा और अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा इसे रजिस्ट्रीकृत या प्रमाजणत, िो भी ििा हो, करने की आवश् यकता पड़ने पर, सूचना प्रौद्योजगकी अजधजनयम, 2000, आधार (जवत्तीय और अन्द् य सहाजयदकयों, प्रसुजवधाओं ओर सेवाओं का लजययत पररिान) अजधजनयम, 2016 और लागू अन्द् य जवजधयों और उनके अधीन बने उन जवजध, जवजधयों, दििाजनिेंिों, अजधसूचनाओं, या पररपत्रों के उपबंधों के अनुसार उसपर इलेक्ट् रॉजनक हस्ट् तािर लगाकर उसे रजिस्ट्रीकृत या प्रमाजणत दकया िाएगा । (2) उपजनयम (1) में जवजनर्िाि इलेक्ट् रॉजनक हस्ट् तािर के अजधप्रमाणन के जलए सूचना प्रौद्योजगकी अजधजनयम, 2000 और अन्द् य सुसंगत जवजधयों और उनके अधीन बने जनयमों, जवजनयमों, दििाजनिेंिों, अजधसूचनाओं, या पररपत्रों के अधीन स्ट् थाजपत प्रदक्रया लागू होगी। 37छ. धारा 120क के अधीन केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा िस्ट् तावेिों का िारीकरण और संप्रेिण - (1) केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार, अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन काया जनष् पािन या कत्ता्‍ यों का जनवाह्न या िजियों का प्रयोग या ऐसा कोई काया करेगा िो अजधजनयम द्वारा केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार को इलेक्ट् रॉजनक माध् यम से जनष् पादित या जनवाह्न या प्रयोग या करने के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, जनिेजित दकया गया हो

[भाग II—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का रािपत्र : असाधारण 9 अजधकारी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संतुष् ट होता है और मतिान केंर में उपजस्ट्थत दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा से कोई आपजत्त नहीं होती है, तो वह मतपत्र पर ही जछदरत अधपन्द् ने पर उक्ट् त सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध का हस्ट् तािर या अंगु े की छाप लेकर उसे मत पत्र िारी करेगा और अधपन्द् ने पर मतपत्र का क्रमांक और अन्द् य जववरण होगा तथा मतपत्र प्राप् त करने के बाि, सिस्ट् य पृथक स्ट् थाजपत मतिान कंपाटामेंट िाएगा और पूरी गोपनीयता के साथ अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों, िो भी ििा हो, के नाम के आगे जिसे वह अपना मत िेना चाहता है, ‘X’ का जचह्न लगाकर अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करके मतपत्र को इस प्रयोिन हेतु रखी मतपेटी में डालेगा । परंतु दक िृजिहीनता या अन्द् य िारीररक दि्‍ यांगता या जनरिरता के कारण यदि कोई सिस्ट् य मतपत्र पर जनिान लगाने में असमथा है तो मतिान अजधकारी, और िहां ऐसे मतिान अजधकारी जनयुक्ट् त नहीं हैं, वहां ररटर्नंग अजधकारी उससे अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों का नाम सुजनजश्चत करेगा जिसके पि में वह अपना मत िेने को इच् छुक है और उसकी ओर से ‘X’ का जनिान लगाकर मतपत्र को मतपेटी में डालेगा । (8) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य जिसका नाम मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों/प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची में प्रजवष् ट है, जिसे मतिान अजधकारी को सुपुिा दकया गया है, को अपना मतिान करने का हक है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को संिर्भात करेगा िो एक संजिप् त िांच करके सोसाइटी के ररकॉडा के संिभा में आपजत्त पर जनणाय करेगा । (9) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा द्वारा दकसी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संबंजधत दकसी आपजत्त पर तब तक जवचार नहीं करेगा िब तक दक आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजि ने प्रत् येक ऐसे मत के जलए 5/- रुपए की फीस का संिाय न कर दिया हो और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी तत् पश् चातम आपजत्त पर जवचार करेगा और मतिान करने आए सिस्ट् य से उसके अंगु े की छाप या हस्ट् तािर, िो भी ििा हो, उसकी पहचान का वणान करने वाली उघोषोिणा पर लेगा और यदि वह ऐसा करने से इंकार करता है तो उसे मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी और यदि िूसरी ओर, ऐसी संजिप् त छानबीन पर ररटर्नंग अजधकारी की संतुजि के अनुसार सिस्ट् य की पहचान स्ट् थाजपत हो िाती है तो मतिान अजधकारी मतपत्र िारी करेगा और सिस्ट् य को तब मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

In last two years, since the formation of Ministry of Cooperation, the cooperative movement has been strengthened due to several path-breaking initiatives of the Ministry. One of the initiatives is creation of National Cooperative Database in coordination with States/UTs Government. The comprehensive national database will comprise data of various kinds of cooperatives–from the lowest unit of the cooperative sector, that is, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to national-level institutions. By systematically verifying the grassroots presence of cooperatives, this sector is becoming more streamlined and effective in its operations. This revolutionary initiative not only facilitates the identification of active cooperative societies, but also assists the Government in the formulation of policies to strengthen the cooperative sector to elevate the standard of living for the underprivileged and marginalized sections of society. 2.2 Need for Database Despite India being home to almost 25% of total cooperative societies in the world and with history of cooperative movement in India dating back to more than a century, there was no comprehensive, authentic and updated data repository in the country about cooperatives, their activities, their members, their financial details etc. The availability of organized database of the cooperatives, can help in formulating programs and schemes, mentioning the exact number of beneficiaries. The Ministry of Cooperation was constituted on 6th July, 2021 with a mandate, inter alia to strengthen cooperative movement in the country and deepening its reach up to grassroots; and creation of appropriate policy, legal and institutional framework to help cooperatives realize their potential. To fulfil this mandate, the process for developing a National Cooperative Database was initiated by the Ministry in consultation with the State/UT Governments, National Cooperative Federations, Central line Ministries and all other Stakeholders at various levels. 2.3 Scope & Benefits of National Cooperative Database The objective of developing National Cooperative Database (NCD) is to provide: • A single point access to authentic and updated information on cooperatives of different sectors and develop a process for better understanding of cooperatives. • The database will function as the main planning tool for Central Ministries, State Governments, Cooperative Federations, Cooperators and Sectoral Institutions like NABARD, etc., for cooperative sector. • The database would also bring synergy among various databases maintained by Central line Ministries and State Governments. • It would also help in identifying gaps/ vacuums in geographical distribution of cooperatives in the country and establishing upward/downward linkages of cooperative societies (Primary to Apex). The National Cooperative Database (NCD) captures data on several parameters related to cooperatives i.e., location details, number of members, economic activities, their upward and downward linkages, level of operations, assets and liabilities, etc. It involved development of a web based secure system to facilitate data feeding from each of the district registrar/functional registrar office which can be viewed and verified by respective state registrar office. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. This revolutionary initiative not only facilitates the identification of active cooperative societies, but also assists the Government in the formulation of policies to strengthen the cooperative sector to elevate the standard of living for the underprivileged and marginalized sections of society. 2.2 Need for Database Despite India being home to almost 25% of total cooperative societies in the world and with history of cooperative movement in India dating back to more than a century, there was no comprehensive, authentic and updated data repository in the country about cooperatives, their activities, their members, their financial details etc. The availability of organized database of the cooperatives, can help in formulating programs and schemes, mentioning the exact number of beneficiaries. The Ministry of Cooperation was constituted on 6th July, 2021 with a mandate, inter alia to strengthen cooperative movement in the country and deepening its reach up to grassroots; and creation of appropriate policy, legal and institutional framework to help cooperatives realize their potential. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has prepared Model Bye-laws to help PACS diversify their activities and become multipurpose cooperative societies. The project aims to bring functional PACS onto an ERP-based common software system and connect them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks. 49 Sector-wise Cooperatives L ong-term rural credit cooperatives were established for providing funds for investment in agriculture – including land development, farm mechanisation and minor irrigation - rural industries and housing. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres (CSCs). Through the CSC framework, PACS can provide various e-governance and citizen-centric services. These can include services related to: * Banking * Insurance * Aadhaar enrolment or updation * Health services * Agricultural services * Government welfare schemes * Other permitted digital services The exact services available at a particular PACS may vary. --- ## Can PACS Become Multipurpose Cooperative Societies? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has prepared Model Bye-laws to help PACS diversify their activities and become multipurpose cooperative societies. The Model Bye-laws enable PACS to undertake more than 25 types of business activities across areas such as agriculture, dairy, fisheries, storage, retail and citizen services. Adoption and implementation are subject to the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act and State-level requirements. --- ## PACS Computerization The Government of India approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS in June 2022. The project aims to bring functional PACS onto an ERP-based common software system and connect them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks. The computerization initiative aims to: * Improve operational efficiency * Speed up loan disbursal * Reduce transaction costs * Improve accounting * Increase transparency * Improve coordination with DCCBs and StCBs --- ## PACS and Farmer Services PACS can act as a local point for farmers to access: * Agricultural credit * Agricultural inputs * Storage facilities * Marketing-related services * Government schemes * Digital citizen services * Other cooperative services The exact services available depend on the PACS and applicable schemes or permissions. --- ## Important Limitation for SIA PACS are governed by applicable cooperative laws and bye-laws. The remitted amount is added in a wallet of the Bank-Branch, CSC-VLE or Insurance Intermediary for onward remittance to the concerned Insurance Company implementing the scheme in a particular geographical area. These partner agencies (Bank Branches, CSC-VLEs & Insurance Intermediaries) can remit the premium amount multiple times to the concerned Insurance Companies before the cut-off-date. For each transaction, a Unique ID (UTR) is assigned using which reconciliation of payments and applications is done by the Insurance Companies. 39.4.3 Add-on Coverage of Crop Risk The State/UT has the option to notify Add-on perils cover with or without Basic Cover (Yield base cover). Selection of risk has been made available on portal as per the provisions available in the guidelines. In the notiﬁcation module, an option has been provided to the States/UTs to select the add-on coverage separately according to the crop and insurance unit along with the Basic Cover as per the notiﬁcation. Claim will be calculated on DigiClaim as per the add-on coverage opted for the crop and IU. 39.4.4 Land Record Integration Land record detail is one of the critical requirements under the PMFBY scheme for validation of insured area. Manual veriﬁcation of the land record data is a sheer challenge. Many State/UTs have digitized land record system, however their hierarchal system and practices are different. DA&FW has moved ahead to integrate the land record system of 10 major states with NCIP to validate the farmer's land parcel with land record system at the time of enrollment under the scheme. State/UTs shares the land record API subsequent to which customization of API consumption for integration of land records of the State(s) with NCIP is executed. The land record details of the farmers is required to be entered during enrolment process and rest of the land details viz. extent of land, ownership share and names of owners/shareholders are fetched through the State/UT land record portal. In the Future, as and when the Agri-Stack system becomes operational, the farmer’s Golden ID along with land records, land area, cadastral maps and sown crop details shall be fetched & validated using it. 39.4.5 Location Master Management

The initiative improves access to affordable medicines in rural areas and provides PACS with an additional economic activity. ### What are the benefits for PACS? PACS operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras can receive applicable trade margins and incentives under the PMBJP framework, subject to current guidelines. ### How many Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been opened through PACS? As of 30 June 2026, 846 Jan Aushadhi Kendras had been opened under PACS across the country. ### How many PACS have received initial approval? As of 30 June 2026, more than 4,250 PACS had received initial approval to open Jan Aushadhi Kendras. ### Is there a State-wise target for PACS Jan Aushadhi Kendras? No. As of the latest official information, there is no State/UT/District-wise target for opening new Jan Aushadhi Kendras through PACS. ### What is the target for Jan Aushadhi Kendras? PACS operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras are eligible for the applicable benefits under PMBJP, including a 30% trade margin on MRP, subject to current guidelines. ### What medicines are covered by the stocking incentive? मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

य सहकारी सोसाइटी का मुख् य कायाकारी ऐसी ररजियों की सूचना, इसके उद्भुत होने के एक सप् ताह के भीतर प्राजधकरण को संसूजचत करेगा, िो अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार ररजियों को भरने की कारावाई करेगा । (2) अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार वैकजल्पक ररजियों में जनयुक्ट् त कोई ्‍ यजि अजधिेि अवजध तक ही बोडा का सिस्ट् य रहेगा, िब तक वह बोडा के सिस्ट् य जिसके स्ट् थान पर जनयुक्ट् त हुआ है, रहेगा । 19य. मतिान की गोपनीयता का अनुरिण - प्रत् येक अजधकारी, जलजपक, अजभकताा या अन्द् य ्‍ यजि िो दकसी जनवााचन में अजभलेखन या मतगणना से िुड़ा काया जनष् पािन कर रहा है, मतगणना की गोपनीयता अनुरजित करेगा और अनुरिण करने में मिि करेगा और दकसी अन्द् य ्‍ यजि को (जसवाए कुछ प्रयोिनों के जलए दकसी जवजध द्वारा या उसके अधीन प्राजधकृत) ऐसी गोपनीयता का उल् लंघन करने के जलए मतिान से संबंजधत कोई सूचना संप्रेजित नहीं करेगा ।” 5. मूल जनयमों में, जनयम 20 के स्ट् थान पर जनम् नजलजखत जनयम रखे िाएंगे, अथाातम: -

पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

Procedure for conduct of elections.— (1) The election of members of the board shall be conducted by a Returning Officer, to be appointed by the Authority and the Returning Officer so appointed shall not be a member or an employee of the multi-State co-operative society: Provided, that the Authority may also appoint one or more persons to be called as the Assistant Returning Officer to assist the Returning Officer, for the conduct of the election to the society. (2) Every Assistant Returning Officer, shall, subject to the control of the Returning Officer and general control of the Authority, be competent to perform all or any of the functions of the Returning Officer: Provided that, no Assistant Returning Officer shall perform the functions of the Returning Officer relating to the scrutiny of nominations unless the Returning Officer is unavoidably prevented from performing the said function. 19H. Procedure for conduct of election to the board of multi-State co-operative societies.—(1) The Chairperson and the Chief Executive of the multi-State co-operative society shall inform the Authority at least six months before the expiry of the term of the board, to conduct elections within time and a copy of the information shall also be sent to the Central Registrar. .
