# Jan Aushadhi Kendras by PACS ## Scheme / Initiative Information - scheme_id: T1-04 - tier: Tier 1 - type: Cooperative sector initiative - official_name: Jan Aushadhi Kendras by PACS - related_scheme: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) - ministry: Ministry of Cooperation / Department of Pharmaceuticals - implementing_agency: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) - sector: Cooperatives / Healthcare / Affordable Medicines - beneficiary_type: PACS and rural communities - state_scope: Pan-India ## Purpose The initiative enables Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to operate Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs). The objective is to improve access to quality generic medicines at affordable prices, particularly in rural areas, while also creating an additional source of income and employment opportunities for PACS. ## Role of PACS PACS can operate Jan Aushadhi Kendras and provide affordable generic medicines to people in their communities. This initiative also helps diversify the economic activities of PACS. ## Benefits The initiative can: 1. Improve access to affordable medicines in rural areas. 2. Provide an additional source of income for PACS. 3. Create employment opportunities. 4. Expand the reach of Jan Aushadhi medicines through the cooperative network. 5. Support affordable healthcare access for rural communities. ## Initial Government Decision In June 2023, the Government decided to allow 2,000 PACS across the country to open Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Jan Aushadhi Kendras. The 2,000 PACS were planned to be identified for opening Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country. ## Current Status As of 30 June 2026, 846 Jan Aushadhi Kendras had been opened under PACS across the country. More than 4,250 PACS had received initial approval to open Jan Aushadhi Kendras. There is no State/UT/District-wise target for opening new Jan Aushadhi Kendras through PACS. The Government has set a target of opening 25,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras by March 2027. ## Benefits Available to PACS Operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras PACS operating Jan Aushadhi Kendras are eligible for the same benefits as other Jan Aushadhi Kendras under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, subject to the applicable guidelines. These include: - 30% trade margin on the Maximum Retail Price (MRP). - Incentives linked to purchases of medicines. - Incentives related to fulfilment of stocking requirements. A special one-time grant of Rs. 2 lakh is available for eligible Jan Aushadhi Kendras in specified priority areas and for specified categories of entrepreneurs, subject to applicable conditions. ## Stocking Requirement / Incentive Since September 2024, stocking of 200 commonly used medicines has been incentivised. The 200 medicines consist of: - 100 top-selling medicines in the scheme product basket. - 100 fast-selling medicines in the market. Jan Aushadhi Kendra owners can receive a monthly incentive based on the stocks maintained for these medicines, subject to applicable guidelines. ## Supply Chain An information-technology-enabled supply chain system is in place for Jan Aushadhi Kendras. www.pmfby.gov.in Operational Guidelines 2023 of PMFBY 158 39.4 Different Modules of NCIP 39.4.1 Integration with Public Fund Management System The NCIP has been integrated with PFMS and a module known as DigiClaim has been developed for managing ﬁnancial transactions to facilitate release of State/UT and GoI share of premium subsidy, Bank Account and AEPS veriﬁcation and payment of insurance claims by the Insurance Companies to the farmers. 39.4.2 Online Remittance of Premium by Financial Institutions A third-party payment gateway has already been integrated with NCIP for the remittance of farmer premium by the Bank branches and other channels partners like CSC eGov & Insurance Intermediaries. The remitted amount is added in a wallet of the Bank-Branch, CSC-VLE or Insurance Intermediary for onward remittance to the concerned Insurance Company implementing the scheme in a particular geographical area. These partner agencies (Bank Branches, CSC-VLEs & Insurance Intermediaries) can remit the premium amount multiple times to the concerned Insurance Companies before the cut-off-date. For each transaction, a Unique ID (UTR) is assigned using which reconciliation of payments and applications is done by the Insurance Companies. 39.4.3 Add-on Coverage of Crop Risk The State/UT has the option to notify Add-on perils cover with or without Basic Cover (Yield base cover). Selection of risk has been made available on portal as per the provisions available in the guidelines. In the notiﬁcation module, an option has been provided to the States/UTs to select the add-on coverage separately according to the crop and insurance unit along with the Basic Cover as per the notiﬁcation. Claim will be calculated on DigiClaim as per the add-on coverage opted for the crop and IU. 39.4.4 Land Record Integration Land record detail is one of the critical requirements under the PMFBY scheme for validation of insured area. Manual veriﬁcation of the land record data is a sheer challenge. Many State/UTs have digitized land record system, however their hierarchal system and practices are different. DA&FW has moved ahead to integrate the land record system of 10 major states with NCIP to validate the farmer's land parcel with land record system at the time of enrollment under the scheme. State/UTs shares the land record API subsequent to which customization of API consumption for integration of land records of the State(s) with NCIP is executed. The land record details of the farmers is required to be entered during enrolment process and rest of the land details viz. extent of land, ownership share and names of owners/shareholders are fetched through the State/UT land record portal. In the Future, as and when the Agri-Stack system becomes operational, the farmer’s Golden ID along with land records, land area, cadastral maps and sown crop details shall be fetched & validated using it. 39.4.5 Location Master Management

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

यजि के वेतन और भत्ते से ऐसी पेंिन की कुल राजि, यदि कोई हो, को घटाकर उसके द्वारा आहरण या आहररत दकया िाएगा । (5) ऑम् बुड्समसमैन द्वारा िौरे पर या स्ट् थानांतरण पर (कायाभार ग्रहण करने के जलए या उसके कायाकाल की समाजप्त पर गृहनगर िाने के जलए की गई यात्रा सजहत) उसके यात्रा भत्ता, िैजनक भत्ते, जनिी सामान के पररवहन और अन्द् य समान मामलों की हकिारी भारत सरकार के जनिेिक के जलए लागू समान वेतनमान और समान िर पर होगी ।

िाने वाले िस्ट् तावेि में हस्ट् तािर करने वाले सिस्ट् य का नाम, पिनाम, पता, सिस्ट् यता संख् या होगा और िो उसके सही होना सुजनजश्चत करेगा और कोई पत्राचार जिसमें मात्र प्राजधकृत हस्ट् तािरकताा जलखकर हस्ट् तािर कर दिया गया हो, को दकसी भी ििा स्ट् वीकारा नहीं िाएगा । 37च. अजधजनयम और उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन िस्ट् तावेिों का इलेक्ट् रॉजनक अनुरिण, पंिीकरण, और प्रमाणन - (1) प्रत् येक आवेिन, जववरणी, ररपोटा, लेखा जववरणी, रजिस्ट् टर, उपजवजधयां या अन्द् य कोई जववरण या िस्ट् तावेि जिसे अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन फाइल या पररचाजलत दकया िाना अपेजित है को केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा इलेक्ट् रॉजनक स्ट् वूपप में अनुरजित दकया िाएगा और अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा इसे रजिस्ट्रीकृत या प्रमाजणत, िो भी ििा हो, करने की आवश् यकता पड़ने पर, सूचना प्रौद्योजगकी अजधजनयम, 2000, आधार (जवत्तीय और अन्द् य सहाजयदकयों, प्रसुजवधाओं ओर सेवाओं का लजययत पररिान) अजधजनयम, 2016 और लागू अन्द् य जवजधयों और उनके अधीन बने उन जवजध, जवजधयों, दििाजनिेंिों, अजधसूचनाओं, या पररपत्रों के उपबंधों के अनुसार उसपर इलेक्ट् रॉजनक हस्ट् तािर लगाकर उसे रजिस्ट्रीकृत या प्रमाजणत दकया िाएगा । (2) उपजनयम (1) में जवजनर्िाि इलेक्ट् रॉजनक हस्ट् तािर के अजधप्रमाणन के जलए सूचना प्रौद्योजगकी अजधजनयम, 2000 और अन्द् य सुसंगत जवजधयों और उनके अधीन बने जनयमों, जवजनयमों, दििाजनिेंिों, अजधसूचनाओं, या पररपत्रों के अधीन स्ट् थाजपत प्रदक्रया लागू होगी। 37छ. धारा 120क के अधीन केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार द्वारा िस्ट् तावेिों का िारीकरण और संप्रेिण - (1) केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार, अजधजनयम या उसके अधीन बने जनयमों के अधीन काया जनष् पािन या कत्ता्‍ यों का जनवाह्न या िजियों का प्रयोग या ऐसा कोई काया करेगा िो अजधजनयम द्वारा केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार को इलेक्ट् रॉजनक माध् यम से जनष् पादित या जनवाह्न या प्रयोग या करने के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, जनिेजित दकया गया हो

ऐसे अभ् यथी जिसका नामांकन स्ट् वीकार दकया गया था, जनवााचन रे होने के पश् चातम ऐसे अभ् यथी की अभ् यर्थाता वापस लेने के नए नोरटस को स्ट् वीकार नहीं दकया िाएगा । 19ध. मतिान के जलए इलेक्ट् रॉजनक मतिान मिीनों तैयार करना - यदि प्राजधकरण मतिान के जलए इलेक्ट् रॉजनक मिीन का उपयोग करने का जनणाय लेता है तो वह इसकी प्रदक्रया जनिेजित करेगा िो िहां तक तकनीकी ूप प से यथािक्ट् य हो, इन जनयमों के अनुसार होगी । 19न. जनवााचन ्‍ यय – जनवााचन संबंधी सभी ्‍ यय जिसमें लेखन सामग्री, मुरण, डाक, फोटोकॉपी, फैक्ट् स, मत पेटी का दकराया, अजमट स्ट् याही, पुजलस सुरिा और अन्द् य ऐसे ्‍ यय की वस्ट् तुओं पर होने वाले ्‍ यय िो बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के प्रजतजनजधयों या जनिेिकों के जनवााचन से संबंजधत है, िैसे मतिाता सूची की तैयारी, यात्रा और अन्द्य भत्ते, और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, सहायक ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, और अन्द्य मतिान कर्मायों को िेय पाररश्रजमक का वहन सोसाइटी द्वारा दकया िाएगा और प्राजधकरण के जनिेि पर प्राजधकरण को भुगतान दकया िाएगा । 19प. जनवााचन ्‍ यय का लेखा - (1) जनवााचन का प्रत् येक अभ् यथी जनवााचन कराने के आिेि की तारीख से उसके पररणाम की घोिणा की तारीख, िोनों तारीख सजम्मजलत, तक जनवााचन से संबंजधत उसके द्वारा या उसके प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि द्वारा दकए गए सभी ्‍ ययों का एक पृथक और सही लेखा पररणाम की घोिणा की तारीख से तीस दिनों की अवजध तक रखेगा । (2) इन लेखों में ऐसी जवजिजियां सजम्मजलत होंगी िो जनयम 19ब में जनर्िाष् ट जववरणों के अजतररक्ट् त समय-समय पर जवजनर्िाष् ट दकए िाएंगे । (3) उक्ट् त ्‍ यय की कुल रकम, प्राजधकरण द्वारा समय-समय पर जवजनर्िाष् ट की गई कुल रकम से अजधक नहीं होगी । (4) जनवााचन लड़ने वाला प्रत् येक अभ् यथी ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के पास अपने जनवााचन ्‍ यय के लेखा को प्राजधकरण द्वारा समय-समय पर जनर्िाष् ट रीजत और समय पर प्रस्ट् तुत करेगा ।

के जलए जनवााजचत होने वाले सिस्ट् यों की संख् या से अजधक है, तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनयत तारीख और समय पर इस प्रयोिन के जलए मतिान कराने की ्‍ यवस्ट् था करेगा और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनवााचन कराने के जलए जितने मतिान अजधकाररयों की आवश् यकता हो, उतनी संख् या में उनकी जनयुजि करेगा । (2) जनवााचन लड़ने वाला अभ् यथी, प्रूपप-IV में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को पत्र द्वारा, िहां मतिान हो रहा है वहां मतिाताओं की पहचान और मतिात पर नज़र रखने के जलए स्ट् वयं का प्रजतजनजधत् व करने हेतु अजभकताा जनयुक्ट् त कर सकता है । ऐसे पत्र में संबंजधत अजभकताा की जलजखत में सहमजत होगी । (3) जनवााचन कराए िाने वाले स्ट् थल पर दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा मतों का पिप्रचार जनिेध होगा । (4) मतिान आरंभ होने के पहले, ररटर्नंग अजधकारी खाली मतपेटी को मतिान आरंभ होने से पूवा उस समय उपजस्ट्थत ्‍ यजियों को दिखाएगा और दफर उसे बंि कर उसपर अपना मुहर इस प्रकार से लगाएगा तादक उसे मुहर तोड़े जबना खोला न िा सके और अभ् यथी या उसका अजभकताा यदि चाहे तो उसपर अपनी मुहर भी लगा सकता है । (5) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध िो अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करना चाहता है को एक मत पत्र दिया िाएगा जिस पर जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों का नाम वणााक्रम में सुजवधा के अनुसार या तो मुदरत, टंदकत या साइक्ट् लोस्ट् टाइल् ड दकया होगा और मतपत्र में सोसाइटी की मुहर भी लगी होगी, और मतपत्र के पीछे ररटर्नंग अजधकारी का आद्यािर भी होगा और इसमें एक स्ट् तंभ भी होगा जिसमें मतिाता जिस ्‍ यजि को अपना मत िेना चाहते हैं, उसके नाम के जवरुद्ध ‘X’का जनिान लगाकर अपना मत िेंगे। (6) प्रत् येक मतिान केंर और िहां एक केन्द् र में एक से अजधक मतिान बूथ हैं, वहां प्रत् येक बूथ में एक पृथक कंपाटामेंट होगा जिसमें सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध गोपनीयता के साथ अपना मत डाल सकते हैं । (7) मतिान करने को इच् छुक प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य सोसाइटी द्वारा उसे दिए गए पहचान पत्र के साथ मतिान केंर में प्रवेि करेगा; मतिान अजधकारी सिस्ट् यों की सूची या मतिान केन्द् र में मतिान करने वाले पात्र सिस्ट् यों या प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची िो उसे उपलब् ध कराई गई है, के संिभा में सिस्ट् य से प्रश् न पूछकर उसकी पहचान करेगा और यदि मतिान

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

[भाग II—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का रािपत्र : असाधारण 9 अजधकारी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संतुष् ट होता है और मतिान केंर में उपजस्ट्थत दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा से कोई आपजत्त नहीं होती है, तो वह मतपत्र पर ही जछदरत अधपन्द् ने पर उक्ट् त सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध का हस्ट् तािर या अंगु े की छाप लेकर उसे मत पत्र िारी करेगा और अधपन्द् ने पर मतपत्र का क्रमांक और अन्द् य जववरण होगा तथा मतपत्र प्राप् त करने के बाि, सिस्ट् य पृथक स्ट् थाजपत मतिान कंपाटामेंट िाएगा और पूरी गोपनीयता के साथ अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों, िो भी ििा हो, के नाम के आगे जिसे वह अपना मत िेना चाहता है, ‘X’ का जचह्न लगाकर अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करके मतपत्र को इस प्रयोिन हेतु रखी मतपेटी में डालेगा । परंतु दक िृजिहीनता या अन्द् य िारीररक दि्‍ यांगता या जनरिरता के कारण यदि कोई सिस्ट् य मतपत्र पर जनिान लगाने में असमथा है तो मतिान अजधकारी, और िहां ऐसे मतिान अजधकारी जनयुक्ट् त नहीं हैं, वहां ररटर्नंग अजधकारी उससे अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों का नाम सुजनजश्चत करेगा जिसके पि में वह अपना मत िेने को इच् छुक है और उसकी ओर से ‘X’ का जनिान लगाकर मतपत्र को मतपेटी में डालेगा । (8) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य जिसका नाम मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों/प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची में प्रजवष् ट है, जिसे मतिान अजधकारी को सुपुिा दकया गया है, को अपना मतिान करने का हक है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को संिर्भात करेगा िो एक संजिप् त िांच करके सोसाइटी के ररकॉडा के संिभा में आपजत्त पर जनणाय करेगा । (9) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा द्वारा दकसी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से (3) एक राष् रीय सहकारी सोसाइटी, अजधजनयम की धारा 120 के उपबंधों के अनुसरण में अपनी जववरजणयां केन्द् रीय रजिस्ट्रार के समि फाइल करेगी जिसमें यह ब् यौरा सजम्मजलत होगा दक- (क) उसने उपयुाक्ट् त उपजनयम (1) के उपबंधों का अनुपालन दकया है, (ख) उसने अजधजनयम की धारा 24 के अधीन संघीय सहकारी सोसाइरटयों के कृत्यों का अनुपालन दकया है । (ग) िेि में सहकारी आंिोलन को सिक्ट् त करने और अपने कायािेत्र में इसकी पहुंच को िमीनी स्ट् तर तक करने के जलए इसने किम उ ाए हैं; और (घ) िेि को जवकजसत करने के जलए अपने सिस्ट् यों के बीच उत्तरिाजयत् व की भावना सजहत अपने कायािेत्र में सहकाररता आधाररत आर्थाक जवकास मॉडल का संवधान करना। 35ख. जद्वतीय अनुसूची से राष् रीय सहकारी सोसाइटी का लोप - अजधजनयम की धारा 116 के उपबंधों के अध् यधीन, केन्द् रीय सरकार दकसी राष् रीय सहकारी सोसाइटी को इन जनयमों के जनयम 35क के उपजनयम (1) के उपबंधों का अनुपालन न करने पर, या अन्द् यथा अकायािील रहने के आधार पर अजधजनयम की जद्वतीय अनुसूची से लोप कर सकती है ।” 10. मूल जनयमों में जनयम 37 के पश् चातम, जनम् नजलजखत जनयमों को अंत्स्ट्थाजपत दकया िाएगा,अथाातम: - “37क. सहकारी सोसाइरटयों में कार्माकों की भती - जवजभन्द् न स्ट् तरों पर कार्माकों की भती एक पारििी, उेेश् यपूणा और पयााप् त ूप प से प्रचाररत प्रजतयोगी प्रदक्रया के अनुसार होगी िो सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट यथोजचत िैजिक और अनुभव मानिंडों के अनुसार होगी । 37ख. गैर-क्रेजडट बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइरटयों के मुख्य कायाकारी की अहाताएं - दकसी गैर-क्रेजडट बहुराज्

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. In last two years, since the formation of Ministry of Cooperation, the cooperative movement has been strengthened due to several path-breaking initiatives of the Ministry. One of the initiatives is creation of National Cooperative Database in coordination with States/UTs Government. The comprehensive national database will comprise data of various kinds of cooperatives–from the lowest unit of the cooperative sector, that is, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to national-level institutions. By systematically verifying the grassroots presence of cooperatives, this sector is becoming more streamlined and effective in its operations. This revolutionary initiative not only facilitates the identification of active cooperative societies, but also assists the Government in the formulation of policies to strengthen the cooperative sector to elevate the standard of living for the underprivileged and marginalized sections of society. 2.2 Need for Database Despite India being home to almost 25% of total cooperative societies in the world and with history of cooperative movement in India dating back to more than a century, there was no comprehensive, authentic and updated data repository in the country about cooperatives, their activities, their members, their financial details etc. The availability of organized database of the cooperatives, can help in formulating programs and schemes, mentioning the exact number of beneficiaries. The Ministry of Cooperation was constituted on 6th July, 2021 with a mandate, inter alia to strengthen cooperative movement in the country and deepening its reach up to grassroots; and creation of appropriate policy, legal and institutional framework to help cooperatives realize their potential. To fulfil this mandate, the process for developing a National Cooperative Database was initiated by the Ministry in consultation with the State/UT Governments, National Cooperative Federations, Central line Ministries and all other Stakeholders at various levels. 2.3 Scope & Benefits of National Cooperative Database The objective of developing National Cooperative Database (NCD) is to provide: • A single point access to authentic and updated information on cooperatives of different sectors and develop a process for better understanding of cooperatives. • The database will function as the main planning tool for Central Ministries, State Governments, Cooperative Federations, Cooperators and Sectoral Institutions like NABARD, etc., for cooperative sector. • The database would also bring synergy among various databases maintained by Central line Ministries and State Governments. • It would also help in identifying gaps/ vacuums in geographical distribution of cooperatives in the country and establishing upward/downward linkages of cooperative societies (Primary to Apex). Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

In last two years, since the formation of Ministry of Cooperation, the cooperative movement has been strengthened due to several path-breaking initiatives of the Ministry. One of the initiatives is creation of National Cooperative Database in coordination with States/UTs Government. The comprehensive national database will comprise data of various kinds of cooperatives–from the lowest unit of the cooperative sector, that is, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to national-level institutions. By systematically verifying the grassroots presence of cooperatives, this sector is becoming more streamlined and effective in its operations. This revolutionary initiative not only facilitates the identification of active cooperative societies, but also assists the Government in the formulation of policies to strengthen the cooperative sector to elevate the standard of living for the underprivileged and marginalized sections of society. 2.2 Need for Database Despite India being home to almost 25% of total cooperative societies in the world and with history of cooperative movement in India dating back to more than a century, there was no comprehensive, authentic and updated data repository in the country about cooperatives, their activities, their members, their financial details etc. The availability of organized database of the cooperatives, can help in formulating programs and schemes, mentioning the exact number of beneficiaries. The Ministry of Cooperation was constituted on 6th July, 2021 with a mandate, inter alia to strengthen cooperative movement in the country and deepening its reach up to grassroots; and creation of appropriate policy, legal and institutional framework to help cooperatives realize their potential. To fulfil this mandate, the process for developing a National Cooperative Database was initiated by the Ministry in consultation with the State/UT Governments, National Cooperative Federations, Central line Ministries and all other Stakeholders at various levels. 2.3 Scope & Benefits of National Cooperative Database The objective of developing National Cooperative Database (NCD) is to provide: • A single point access to authentic and updated information on cooperatives of different sectors and develop a process for better understanding of cooperatives. • The database will function as the main planning tool for Central Ministries, State Governments, Cooperative Federations, Cooperators and Sectoral Institutions like NABARD, etc., for cooperative sector. • The database would also bring synergy among various databases maintained by Central line Ministries and State Governments. • It would also help in identifying gaps/ vacuums in geographical distribution of cooperatives in the country and establishing upward/downward linkages of cooperative societies (Primary to Apex). The National Cooperative Database (NCD) captures data on several parameters related to cooperatives i.e., location details, number of members, economic activities, their upward and downward linkages, level of operations, assets and liabilities, etc. It involved development of a web based secure system to facilitate data feeding from each of the district registrar/functional registrar office which can be viewed and verified by respective state registrar office. Obtain the membership application form or use the available online registration facility, where implemented. 4. Complete the required KYC and submit the required documents. 5. Submit identity, residence, land-holding or other applicable proof as required. 6. Pay the applicable admission fee and share contribution, if required. 7. The application may be placed before the Board of Directors for a decision according to the applicable bye-laws. 8. If approved, complete the remaining membership formalities. Under the Model Bye-laws, the Board of Directors decides the membership application within the prescribed period, and the applicant is informed of the decision according to the applicable procedure. The exact process, eligibility, documents, fees and share requirements may differ between States and individual PACS. ### PACS Membership Documents – Multilingual Retrieval Terms English: What documents are required to join PACS? Yes. PACS directly deal with rural and agricultural borrowers and provide credit. PACS traditionally provide short-term and medium-term agricultural credit to member farmers. Loan availability, amount, interest rate, repayment period, collateral requirements and eligibility depend on the applicable rules and the concerned cooperative credit institution. SIA should verify current loan conditions before giving specific financial figures. --- ## What Agricultural Inputs Can PACS Provide? PACS may provide or distribute agricultural inputs such as: * Seeds * Fertilizers * Pesticides They may also provide other agricultural services depending on their activities and applicable rules. --- ## Can PACS Provide Storage Services? Yes. PACS can undertake storage and warehousing-related activities. The Model Bye-laws support diversification of PACS into activities such as godowns, warehousing and food-grain procurement. Individual availability depends on the PACS, local implementation and applicable permissions. --- ## Can PACS Function as Common Service Centres? Yes. The Ministry of Cooperation has enabled PACS to function as Common Service Centres (CSCs). Through the CSC framework, PACS can provide various e-governance and citizen-centric services. These

top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. Voluntary and Open Membership.—Co-operatives are voluntary organisations, open to all persons capable of using their services and willing to accept the responsibilities of membership, without discrimination on bases of gender, social inequality, racial, political ideologies or religious consideration. 2. Democratic Member Control.—Co-operatives are democratic organisations controlled by their members, who actively participate in setting their policies and decision making. Elected representatives of these co-operatives are responsible and accountable to their members. 3. Member’s Economic Participation.—Members contribute equitably and control the capital of their Co-operative democratically. At least a part of the surplus arising out of the economic results would be the common property of the co-operatives. The remaining surplus could be utilised benefiting the members in proportion to their share in the Co-operative. 4. Autonomy and Independence.—Co-operatives are autonomous, self-help organisations controlled by their members. If co-operatives enter into agreement with other organisations including Government or raise capital from external sources, they do so on terms that ensure their democratic control by members and maintenance of Co-operative autonomy. 5. Education, Training and Information.—Co-operatives provide education and training to their members, elected representatives and employees so that they can contribute effectively to the development of their Co-operatives. They also make the general public, particularly young people and leaders aware of the nature and benefits of co-operation. 6. Co-operation among Co-operatives.—Co-operatives serve their members most effectively and strengthen the co-operative movement, by working together through available local, regional, national and international structures. 7. Concern for Community.—While focusing on the needs of their members, co-operatives work for the sustainable development of communities through policies accepted by their members.

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

ही जछदरत अधपन्द् ने पर उक्ट् त सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध का हस्ट् तािर या अंगु े की छाप लेकर उसे मत पत्र िारी करेगा और अधपन्द् ने पर मतपत्र का क्रमांक और अन्द् य जववरण होगा तथा मतपत्र प्राप् त करने के बाि, सिस्ट् य पृथक स्ट् थाजपत मतिान कंपाटामेंट िाएगा और पूरी गोपनीयता के साथ अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों, िो भी ििा हो, के नाम के आगे जिसे वह अपना मत िेना चाहता है, ‘X’ का जचह्न लगाकर अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करके मतपत्र को इस प्रयोिन हेतु रखी मतपेटी में डालेगा । परंतु दक िृजिहीनता या अन्द् य िारीररक दि्‍ यांगता या जनरिरता के कारण यदि कोई सिस्ट् य मतपत्र पर जनिान लगाने में असमथा है तो मतिान अजधकारी, और िहां ऐसे मतिान अजधकारी जनयुक्ट् त नहीं हैं, वहां ररटर्नंग अजधकारी उससे अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों का नाम सुजनजश्चत करेगा जिसके पि में वह अपना मत िेने को इच् छुक है और उसकी ओर से ‘X’ का जनिान लगाकर मतपत्र को मतपेटी में डालेगा । (8) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य जिसका नाम मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों/प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची में प्रजवष् ट है, जिसे मतिान अजधकारी को सुपुिा दकया गया है, को अपना मतिान करने का हक है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को संिर्भात करेगा िो एक संजिप् त िांच करके सोसाइटी के ररकॉडा के संिभा में आपजत्त पर जनणाय करेगा । (9) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा द्वारा दकसी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संबंजधत दकसी आपजत्त पर तब तक जवचार नहीं करेगा िब तक दक आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजि ने प्रत् येक ऐसे मत के जलए 5/- रुपए की फीस का संिाय न कर दिया हो और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी तत् पश् चातम आपजत्त पर जवचार करेगा और मतिान करने आए सिस्ट् य से उसके अंगु े की छाप या हस्ट् तािर, िो भी ििा हो, उसकी पहचान का वणान करने वाली उघोषोिणा पर लेगा और यदि वह ऐसा करने से इंकार करता है तो उसे मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी और यदि िूसरी ओर, ऐसी संजिप् त छानबीन पर ररटर्नंग अजधकारी की संतुजि के अनुसार सिस्ट् य की पहचान स्ट् थाजपत हो िाती है तो मतिान अजधकारी मतपत्र िारी करेगा और सिस्ट् य को तब मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी Compliance with sections 43 and 44 of the Act.— The eligibility of the candidates for the election of members of the board and office bearers shall be subject to the provisions contained in sections 43 and 44 of the Act. 19L. Scrutiny of nomination papers.—(1) On the day fixed for the scrutiny of nomination papers,— (a) the Returning Officer shall, at the appointed hours, take up the scrutiny of nomination Forms and the candidate or the proposer or seconder of each of the candidates may be present at the time and place when nomination papers are scrutinised; (b) the Returning Officer shall examine the nomination Forms and shall decide all objections which may be made by any candidate or his proposer or seconder in respect of any nomination and may, either accept or reject any nomination: Provided that the nomination of a candidate shall not be rejected on the ground of an incorrect description of his name or the name of his proposer or seconder or of any other particulars relating to the candidate or his proposer or seconder, as entered in the list of members; if the identity of the candidate, proposer or seconder, as the case may be, is established beyond reasonable doubt; (c) the Returning Officer shall endorse on each nomination Form his decision of accepting or rejecting the same, as the case may be, and if the nomination paper is rejected, he shall record in writing a brief statement of his reasons for such rejection; (d) the Returning Officer shall not allow any adjournment of the proceedings except when proceedings are interrupted or obstructed by a riot or affray or by any other cause beyond his control; and (e) list of valid nominations accepted by the Returning Officer shall be published on the notice board of the society containing the names in the alphabetical order in English and address of the candidates as given in the nomination paper. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. In last two years, since the formation of Ministry of Cooperation, the cooperative movement has been strengthened due to several path-breaking initiatives of the Ministry. One of the initiatives is creation of National Cooperative Database in coordination with States/UTs Government. The comprehensive national database will comprise data of various kinds of cooperatives–from the lowest unit of the cooperative sector, that is, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) to national-level institutions. By systematically verifying the grassroots presence of cooperatives, this sector is becoming more streamlined and effective in its operations. This revolutionary initiative not only facilitates the identification of active cooperative societies, but also assists the Government in the formulation of policies to strengthen the cooperative sector to elevate the standard of living for the underprivileged and marginalized sections of society. 2.2 Need for Database Despite India being home to almost 25% of total cooperative societies in the world and with history of cooperative movement in India dating back to more than a century, there was no comprehensive, authentic and updated data repository in the country about cooperatives, their activities, their members, their financial details etc. The availability of organized database of the cooperatives, can help in formulating programs and schemes, mentioning the exact number of beneficiaries. The Ministry of Cooperation was constituted on 6th July, 2021 with a mandate, inter alia to strengthen cooperative movement in the country and deepening its reach up to grassroots; and creation of appropriate policy, legal and institutional framework to help cooperatives realize their potential. To fulfil this mandate, the process for developing a National Cooperative Database was initiated by the Ministry in consultation with the State/UT Governments, National Cooperative Federations, Central line Ministries and all other Stakeholders at various levels. 2.3 Scope & Benefits of National Cooperative Database The objective of developing National Cooperative Database (NCD) is to provide: • A single point access to authentic and updated information on cooperatives of different sectors and develop a process for better understanding of cooperatives. • The database will function as the main planning tool for Central Ministries, State Governments, Cooperative Federations, Cooperators and Sectoral Institutions like NABARD, etc., for cooperative sector. • The database would also bring synergy among various databases maintained by Central line Ministries and State Governments. • It would also help in identifying gaps/ vacuums in geographical distribution of cooperatives in the country and establishing upward/downward linkages of cooperative societies (Primary to Apex). The National Cooperative Database (NCD) captures data on several parameters related to cooperatives i.e., location details, number of members, economic activities, their upward and downward linkages, level of operations, assets and liabilities, etc. It involved development of a web based secure system to facilitate data feeding from each of the district registrar/functional registrar office which can be viewed and verified by respective state registrar office. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. To bring in efficiency, accountability, transparency at PACS and improve profitability. b. To bring in accuracy and uniformity in the conduct of business, accounting with

49 Sector-wise Cooperatives L ong-term rural credit cooperatives were established for providing funds for investment in agriculture – including land development, farm mechanisation and minor irrigation - rural industries and housing. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives
