35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. 52 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report C redit and Thrift Societies are member-driven financial institutions registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of various states in India. They play a very significant role in meeting credit needs of poor and marginalized sections of the society. They offer customized loan products and repayment schedules based on members’ needs and income levels and foster a sense of community and social responsibility among members. In India, there are 79,795 primary credit and thrift societies in 34 States, except for Ladakh and Kerala, with 4.32 crore members. Out of 79,795 societies, 66,713 societies are functional, 10,489 are dormant and 2,593 are under liquidation. Around 56% societies i.e., 44,404 are operating in urban areas and the remaining 35,391 societies are operating in rural areas. Telangana and Maharashtra have the maximum number of credit and thrift societies. Approximately 55% of the total primary credit and thrift societies are operating in these two states alone. The remaining 45% of the societies are operating in 32 states. Telangana state has the highest number of societies i.e., 24,020 with a membership base of 47.77 lakh followed by Maharashtra which has 20,337 societies with 2.27 crore members. The core functions of these societies are: • Thrift: Encouraging members to save regularly through deposits, often with attractive interest rates compared to traditional savings accounts. • Credit: Providing loans to members for various purposes like education, medical expenses, business ventures, or agricultural needs, often at lower interest rates than commercial banks. • Other Services: Many societies offer additional services like micro-insurance, money transfers, and financial literacy programs. 49 Sector-wise Cooperatives L ong-term rural credit cooperatives were established for providing funds for investment in agriculture – including land development, farm mechanisation and minor irrigation - rural industries and housing. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. 56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

SIA should not give a fixed loan amount or interest rate unless it has a verified current official source. --- ## How Does PACS Connect With NABARD and Cooperative Banks? PACS form the grassroots level of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. The higher levels include: 1. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) 2. District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) 3. State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) NABARD supports and refinances the cooperative credit system through the higher cooperative banking structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. --- ## Who Can Become a PACS Member? Membership of a PACS is governed by the applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, rules and the society's bye-laws. Therefore, there is no single universal membership rule or document list that applies identically to every PACS in India. A person interested in becoming a PACS member should check: * The applicable State cooperative law * The PACS bye-laws * The membership eligibility conditions * The local PACS office * Any required membership or share contribution * Documents required by the concerned PACS ### PACS Membership – Retrieval Terms English: Who can become a PACS member? ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

ही जछदरत अधपन्द् ने पर उक्ट् त सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध का हस्ट् तािर या अंगु े की छाप लेकर उसे मत पत्र िारी करेगा और अधपन्द् ने पर मतपत्र का क्रमांक और अन्द् य जववरण होगा तथा मतपत्र प्राप् त करने के बाि, सिस्ट् य पृथक स्ट् थाजपत मतिान कंपाटामेंट िाएगा और पूरी गोपनीयता के साथ अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों, िो भी ििा हो, के नाम के आगे जिसे वह अपना मत िेना चाहता है, ‘X’ का जचह्न लगाकर अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करके मतपत्र को इस प्रयोिन हेतु रखी मतपेटी में डालेगा । परंतु दक िृजिहीनता या अन्द् य िारीररक दि्‍ यांगता या जनरिरता के कारण यदि कोई सिस्ट् य मतपत्र पर जनिान लगाने में असमथा है तो मतिान अजधकारी, और िहां ऐसे मतिान अजधकारी जनयुक्ट् त नहीं हैं, वहां ररटर्नंग अजधकारी उससे अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों का नाम सुजनजश्चत करेगा जिसके पि में वह अपना मत िेने को इच् छुक है और उसकी ओर से ‘X’ का जनिान लगाकर मतपत्र को मतपेटी में डालेगा । (8) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य जिसका नाम मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों/प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची में प्रजवष् ट है, जिसे मतिान अजधकारी को सुपुिा दकया गया है, को अपना मतिान करने का हक है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को संिर्भात करेगा िो एक संजिप् त िांच करके सोसाइटी के ररकॉडा के संिभा में आपजत्त पर जनणाय करेगा । (9) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा द्वारा दकसी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संबंजधत दकसी आपजत्त पर तब तक जवचार नहीं करेगा िब तक दक आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजि ने प्रत् येक ऐसे मत के जलए 5/- रुपए की फीस का संिाय न कर दिया हो और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी तत् पश् चातम आपजत्त पर जवचार करेगा और मतिान करने आए सिस्ट् य से उसके अंगु े की छाप या हस्ट् तािर, िो भी ििा हो, उसकी पहचान का वणान करने वाली उघोषोिणा पर लेगा और यदि वह ऐसा करने से इंकार करता है तो उसे मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

Scrutiny of nomination papers.—(1) On the day fixed for the scrutiny of nomination papers,— (a) the Returning Officer shall, at the appointed hours, take up the scrutiny of nomination Forms and the candidate or the proposer or seconder of each of the candidates may be present at the time and place when nomination papers are scrutinised; (b) the Returning Officer shall examine the nomination Forms and shall decide all objections which may be made by any candidate or his proposer or seconder in respect of any nomination and may, either accept or reject any nomination: Provided that the nomination of a candidate shall not be rejected on the ground of an incorrect description of his name or the name of his proposer or seconder or of any other particulars relating to the candidate or his proposer or seconder, as entered in the list of members; if the identity of the candidate, proposer or seconder, as the case may be, is established beyond reasonable doubt; (c) the Returning Officer shall endorse on each nomination Form his decision of accepting or rejecting the same, as the case may be, and if the nomination paper is rejected, he shall record in writing a brief statement of his reasons for such rejection; (d) the Returning Officer shall not allow any adjournment of the proceedings except when proceedings are interrupted or obstructed by a riot or affray or by any other cause beyond his control; and (e) list of valid nominations accepted by the Returning Officer shall be published on the notice board of the society containing the names in the alphabetical order in English and address of the candidates as given in the nomination paper. results.retrieved_text: मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

पर भी चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस नोरटस में जनम् नजलजखत सूचनाएं होंगी, अथाातम: (क) जनवााचन द्वारा भरी िाने वाली ररजियों की संख् या ; (ख) जनवााचन का िेत्र (उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट) जिसमें से सिस्ट् यों का जनवााचन दकया िाना है ; (ग) बोडा की सिस्ट् यता की पात्रता हेतु उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट अहाताएं, यदि कोई हैं ; (घ) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी का नाम, तारीख, स्ट् थान और समय जिस िौरान सिस्ट् यों द्वारा नामांकन कागज़ भरा िाएगा, वह तारीख िो जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख से न्द् यूनतम स्ट् पष् ट एक दिन पहले हो या यदि वह एक अवकाि का दिन है तो उससे पूवावती दिन िो सावािजनक अवकाि न हो । स्ट् पष् टीकरण- इस जनयम के प्रयोिन से िब् ि ‘सावािजनक अवकाि’ से ऐसा कोई दिन अजभप्रेत है िो परक्राम् य जलखत अजधजनयम, 1981 (1881 का 26) की धारा 25 के अधीन या ऐसा कोई दिन िो केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार द्वारा, िो भी ििा हो, केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार के कायाालयों के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, सावािजनक अवकाि के ूपप में अजधसूजचत की गई हो ; (ङ) वह तारीख और वह समय और स्ट् थान िब नामांकन कागिों की िांच की िाएगी; और (च) वह तारीख और समय तथा वह स्ट् थान और समय िब मतिान होगा । 19-स. सिस्ट् यों और प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची को तैयार करना - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा उस तारीख के अनुसार िो मतिान के जलए जनयत तारीख से तीस दिन पूवा मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों की सूची तैयार की िाएगी और सूची की प्रजतजलजपयों को सोसाइटी के कारबार के मूल स्ट् थान और इसकी सभी िाखाओं, यदि कोई हो, के नोरटस बोडा पर जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख के न्द् यूनतम पंरह दिन पूवा चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस सूची में जनम् नजलजखत जवजनर्िाष् ट होंगे - (क) सिस्ट् य का िाजखला संख् या और नाम, जपता या पजत का नाम, और व्यजिक की ििा में ऐसे सिस्ट् य का पता; और

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

यजि के वेतन और भत्ते से ऐसी पेंिन की कुल राजि, यदि कोई हो, को घटाकर उसके द्वारा आहरण या आहररत दकया िाएगा । (5) ऑम् बुड्समसमैन द्वारा िौरे पर या स्ट् थानांतरण पर (कायाभार ग्रहण करने के जलए या उसके कायाकाल की समाजप्त पर गृहनगर िाने के जलए की गई यात्रा सजहत) उसके यात्रा भत्ता, िैजनक भत्ते, जनिी सामान के पररवहन और अन्द् य समान मामलों की हकिारी भारत सरकार के जनिेिक के जलए लागू समान वेतनमान और समान िर पर होगी ।

(4) The Returning Officer shall, at the close of the time fixed for the receipt of nomination Forms, prepare and display on the notice board of the society, a list of nominations received by him and any nomination Form submitted after the date and time fixed for its receipt, shall be rejected. (5) No person shall be nominated as a candidate for election to fill a seat on the board if he— (a) is ineligible to vote; (b) is not qualified or is disqualified to be the member of a multi-State co-operative society or a member of the board under the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder; and (c) does not possess the necessary qualifications specified in the bye-laws of the society for election as member of the board. 19K. Compliance with sections 43 and 44 of the Act.— The eligibility of the candidates for the election of members of the board and office bearers shall be subject to the provisions contained in sections 43 and 44 of the Act. 19L. Scrutiny of nomination papers.—(1) On the day fixed for the scrutiny of nomination papers,— (a) the Returning Officer shall, at the appointed hours, take up the scrutiny of nomination Forms and the candidate or the proposer or seconder of each of the candidates may be present at the time and place when nomination papers are scrutinised; (b) the Returning Officer shall examine the nomination Forms and shall decide all objections which may be made by any candidate or his proposer or seconder in respect of any nomination and may, either accept or reject any nomination: Provided that the nomination of a candidate shall not be rejected on the ground of an incorrect description of his name or the name of his proposer or seconder or of any other particulars relating to the candidate or his proposer or seconder, as entered in the list of members; if the identity of the candidate, proposer or seconder, as the case may be, is established beyond reasonable doubt; (c) the Returning Officer shall endorse on each nomination Form his decision of accepting or rejecting the same, as the case may be, and if the nomination paper is rejected, he shall record in writing a brief statement of his reasons for such rejection; (d) the Returning Officer shall not allow any adjournment of the proceedings except when proceedings are interrupted or obstructed by a riot or affray or by any other cause beyond his control; and (e) list of valid nominations accepted by the Returning Officer shall be published on the notice board of the society containing the names in the alphabetical order in English and address of the candidates as given in the nomination paper. पर भी चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस नोरटस में जनम् नजलजखत सूचनाएं होंगी, अथाातम: (क) जनवााचन द्वारा भरी िाने वाली ररजियों की संख् या ; (ख) जनवााचन का िेत्र (उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट) जिसमें से सिस्ट् यों का जनवााचन दकया िाना है ; (ग) बोडा की सिस्ट् यता की पात्रता हेतु उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट अहाताएं, यदि कोई हैं ; (घ) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी का नाम, तारीख, स्ट् थान और समय जिस िौरान सिस्ट् यों द्वारा नामांकन कागज़ भरा िाएगा, वह तारीख िो जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख से न्द् यूनतम स्ट् पष् ट एक दिन पहले हो या यदि वह एक अवकाि का दिन है तो उससे पूवावती दिन िो सावािजनक अवकाि न हो । स्ट् पष् टीकरण- इस जनयम के प्रयोिन से िब् ि ‘सावािजनक अवकाि’ से ऐसा कोई दिन अजभप्रेत है िो परक्राम् य जलखत अजधजनयम, 1981 (1881 का 26) की धारा 25 के अधीन या ऐसा कोई दिन िो केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार द्वारा, िो भी ििा हो, केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार के कायाालयों के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, सावािजनक अवकाि के ूपप में अजधसूजचत की गई हो ; (ङ) वह तारीख और वह समय और स्ट् थान िब नामांकन कागिों की िांच की िाएगी; और (च) वह तारीख और समय तथा वह स्ट् थान और समय िब मतिान होगा । 19-स. सिस्ट् यों और प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची को तैयार करना - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा उस तारीख के अनुसार िो मतिान के जलए जनयत तारीख से तीस दिन पूवा मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों की सूची तैयार की िाएगी और सूची की प्रजतजलजपयों को सोसाइटी के कारबार के मूल स्ट् थान और इसकी सभी िाखाओं, यदि कोई हो, के नोरटस बोडा पर जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख के न्द् यूनतम पंरह दिन पूवा चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस सूची में जनम् नजलजखत जवजनर्िाष् ट होंगे - (क) सिस्ट् य का िाजखला संख् या और नाम, जपता या पजत का नाम, और व्यजिक की ििा में ऐसे सिस्ट् य का पता; और

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

[भाग II—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का रािपत्र : असाधारण 9 अजधकारी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संतुष् ट होता है और मतिान केंर में उपजस्ट्थत दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा से कोई आपजत्त नहीं होती है, तो वह मतपत्र पर ही जछदरत अधपन्द् ने पर उक्ट् त सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध का हस्ट् तािर या अंगु े की छाप लेकर उसे मत पत्र िारी करेगा और अधपन्द् ने पर मतपत्र का क्रमांक और अन्द् य जववरण होगा तथा मतपत्र प्राप् त करने के बाि, सिस्ट् य पृथक स्ट् थाजपत मतिान कंपाटामेंट िाएगा और पूरी गोपनीयता के साथ अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों, िो भी ििा हो, के नाम के आगे जिसे वह अपना मत िेना चाहता है, ‘X’ का जचह्न लगाकर अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करके मतपत्र को इस प्रयोिन हेतु रखी मतपेटी में डालेगा । परंतु दक िृजिहीनता या अन्द् य िारीररक दि्‍ यांगता या जनरिरता के कारण यदि कोई सिस्ट् य मतपत्र पर जनिान लगाने में असमथा है तो मतिान अजधकारी, और िहां ऐसे मतिान अजधकारी जनयुक्ट् त नहीं हैं, वहां ररटर्नंग अजधकारी उससे अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों का नाम सुजनजश्चत करेगा जिसके पि में वह अपना मत िेने को इच् छुक है और उसकी ओर से ‘X’ का जनिान लगाकर मतपत्र को मतपेटी में डालेगा । (8) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य जिसका नाम मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों/प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची में प्रजवष् ट है, जिसे मतिान अजधकारी को सुपुिा दकया गया है, को अपना मतिान करने का हक है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को संिर्भात करेगा िो एक संजिप् त िांच करके सोसाइटी के ररकॉडा के संिभा में आपजत्त पर जनणाय करेगा । (9) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा द्वारा दकसी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संबंजधत दकसी आपजत्त पर तब तक जवचार नहीं करेगा िब तक दक आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजि ने प्रत् येक ऐसे मत के जलए 5/- रुपए की फीस का संिाय न कर दिया हो और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी तत् पश् चातम आपजत्त पर जवचार करेगा और मतिान करने आए सिस्ट् य से उसके अंगु े की छाप या हस्ट् तािर, िो भी ििा हो, उसकी पहचान का वणान करने वाली उघोषोिणा पर लेगा और यदि वह ऐसा करने से इंकार करता है तो उसे मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी 56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

results.retrieved_text: 3 Financial Literacy - Guidance note for trainers 1. The objective of conduct of financial literacy camps is to facilitate financial inclusion through provision of two essentials i.e. literacy and easy access. It should aim at imparting knowledge to enable financial planning, inculcate saving habits and improve the understanding of financial products leading to effective use of financial services by the common man. Financial literacy should help them plan ahead of time for their life cycle needs and deal with unexpected emergencies without resorting to debt. They should be able to proactively manage money and avoid debt traps. In order to ensure that the knowledge provided through awareness results in inculcating banking habits, literacy inputs need to be synchronized with access to financial services so as to enable the common man to use the information effectively to gain control over financial matters. It should also result in enhancement of their economic security aided by use of banking services. 2. The banks as providers of financial services, have an inherent gain in the spread of financial inclusion and financial literacy, as it would help them capture the untapped business opportunities. Small customer is the key and banks should harness the business opportunities available at the bottom of the pyramid. Hence banks must view the financial literacy efforts as their future investments. Banks must provide a bouquet of banking services comprising of a small overdraft facility, variable recurring deposit account, KCC, remittance facilities to the account holders in order to make the accounts transactional. People should be encouraged to make transactions in these accounts so that the cost of maintaining the accounts is recovered to make it a viable and profitable business of the banks. The provision of adequate credit is also important not only in the interest of the customer, but also for the banks as the income earned through interest earned would make the exercise a commercially viable proposition. Banks must provide credit at a competitive though non exploitative rate but certainly not at a subsidised rate. 3. Creating awareness and knowledge about various products and providing these products at their doorstep would be the first step in capturing the accounts. The objective of Financial Literacy Guide is to create awareness and educate masses in a lucid manner about management of money, importance of savings, advantages of saving with banks, other facilities provided by banks and benefits of borrowing from banks. This guide is a ready reckoner for trainers involved in Financial Literacy and Financial Inclusion. It should be used

Keeping in view of the extent of exclusion, banks need to conduct these Financial Literacy Camps in a mission mode, with the ultimate objective of making financial inclusion a viable business model by capturing the untapped business opportunities. In accordance with the objectives as stated above, it is necessary to evaluate the effectiveness of financial literacy efforts in linking the excluded segment to the banking system. SLBCs/DCC would review the financial literacy efforts undertaken by FLCs and rural branches under their jurisdiction, as a regular agenda item in the SLBC/DCC meetings. The details of FLCs along with contact details should be published on the respective SLBC website. Similarly Banks’ Head Offices would review the effectiveness of financial literacy efforts undertaken by their FLCs and rural branches. A structured monitoring mechanism both for FLCs and rural branches would be put in place shortly. 4. Banks’ Top Management including CMDs should ensure that all the rural branches and FLCs prepare a calendar for conduct of Financial Literacy Camps in the beginning of the year. They should give wide publicity to the financial literacy drive by attending some of the Financial Literacy Camps conducted by rural branches and FLCs during their outreach visits. In order to ensure consistency in the messages reaching the target audience of financially excluded people during the Financial Literacy Camps, it is necessary for banks to use the Financial Literacy Guide as a standard curriculum to impart basic conceptual understanding of financial products and services. They may also consider converting the contents of this guide into plays, skits, videos, films etc, for use in the Financial Literacy Camps. 5 Conduct of Financial Literacy Camps- Operational Guidelines All the Financial Literacy Centres and rural branches should prepare an annual calendar of locations for conduct of outdoor Financial Literacy Camps. At every location, the program should be conducted in three stages to be spread over a period of three months comprising of three sessions of minimum two hours each plus a visit to ensure timely delivery of cards. Suitable premises or open place for conduct of program should be identified in advance. Banks may customize the program depending upon the requirement of a particular location and available resources. In all circumstances, the underlying objective of the conduct of program should be to bring the maximum number of participants into the banking fold. First Session  The first session would mainly focus on creating awareness on financial concepts, personal finance and management of money amongst the people. For this purpose, bank should organize a camp for a group of villagers. Advance publicity should be given in the village about the conduct of the camp to ensure good attendance by the villagers.  The work of organizing the camp should be taken up beforehand with the involvement of prominent persons of the area like village sarpanch, school teachers or any other person having good rapport with the villagers. Suitable arrangements may be made at the place identified for the conduct of the program. All the charts and play cards should be placed before the arrival of the participants.  Prepare a list of participants with details of name, age, occupation etc.  Topics to be covered should be financial planning, budgeting, savings, how to maintain financial diary, advantages of saving with banks, the concept of a Business Correspondent, difference between formal and informal sources of borrowing, purpose and cost of borrowing, different types of borrowing etc, as given in the guide.  Distribute a financial diary to each of the participants. Explain how to use the financial diary for preparing the budget and maintaining periodical accounts. Reiterate the advantages of maintaining the diary. Ask them to use diary at home for preparing their budget and writing income and expenses for one month. Advise them to bring the diary when they come for the next session.

It should aim at imparting knowledge to enable financial planning, inculcate saving habits and improve the understanding of financial products leading to effective use of financial services by the common man. In accordance with the objectives as stated above, it is necessary to evaluate the effectiveness of financial literacy efforts in linking the excluded segment to the banking system. 5 Conduct of Financial Literacy Camps- Operational Guidelines All the Financial Literacy Centres and rural branches should prepare an annual calendar of locations for conduct of outdoor Financial Literacy Camps. At every location, the program should be conducted in three stages to be spread over a period of three months comprising of three sessions of minimum two hours each plus a visit to ensure timely delivery of cards. Suitable premises or open place for conduct of program should be identified in advance. Banks may customize the program depending upon the requirement of a particular location and available resources. In all circumstances, the underlying objective of the conduct of program should be to bring the maximum number of participants into the banking fold. First Session  The first session would mainly focus on creating awareness on financial concepts, personal finance and management of money amongst the people. For this purpose, bank should organize a camp for a group of villagers. Advance publicity should be given in the village about the conduct of the camp to ensure good attendance by the villagers.  The work of organizing the camp should be taken up beforehand with the involvement of prominent persons of the area like village sarpanch, school teachers or any other person having good rapport with the villagers. Suitable arrangements may be made at the place identified for the conduct of the program. All the charts and play cards should be placed before the arrival of the participants.  Prepare a list of participants with details of name, age, occupation etc.  Topics to be covered should be financial planning, budgeting, savings, how to maintain financial diary, advantages of saving with banks, the concept of a Business Correspondent, difference between formal and informal sources of borrowing, purpose and cost of borrowing, different types of borrowing etc, as given in the guide.  Distribute a financial diary to each of the participants. Explain how to use the financial diary for preparing the budget and maintaining periodical accounts. Reiterate the advantages of maintaining the diary. Ask them to use diary at home for preparing their budget and writing income and expenses for one month. Advise them to bring the diary when they come for the next session.

Multi-State co-operative societies which may be registered.—(1) No multi-State co-operative society shall be registered under this Act, unless,— (a) its main objects are to serve the interests of members in more than one state; and (b) its bye-laws provide for social and economic betterment of its members through self-help and mutual aid in accordance with the co-operative principles. As advised therein, we have now prepared a comprehensive Financial Literacy Guide containing Guidance Note for Trainers, Operational Guidelines for conduct of Financial Literacy Camps & Financial Literacy Material as also a Financial Diary and a set of 16 posters as explained below. To start with, the entire material has been prepared in Hindi and English. It will also be translated in other Indian languages in due course of time.  The Financial Literacy Guide contains operational guidelines which clearly spell out the manner in which Financial Literacy Camps should be conducted so as to synchronise it with providing financial access and thus linking the financially excluded section with the banking system. The objective of Financial Literacy material is to aid creating financial awareness and educate common people on management of money, importance of savings, advantages of saving with banks, other facilities provided by banks and benefits of borrowing from banks. This guide is a ready reckoner for trainers involved in Financial Literacy and Financial Inclusion.  The Financial Diary has been prepared for distribution to the target audience with the objective of enabling them to keep a record of their income and expenses leading to better financial planning and understanding of how they spend.  The posters with simple and appealing slogans, which communicate the messages of money management, savings, borrowings and basic banking products pictorially, may be displayed prominently before, during and after the Financial Literacy Camps.

This Committee will be headed by the District Magistrate (DM*)/Collector and the representatives of Farmers, Lead District Manager (LDM/Banks, District Development Manager (DDM) NABARD, Insurance Company and concerned District Authority/Department (i.e, Agriculture/Horticulture/Cooperative/Revenue/ Agricultural Statistics etc.) shall be appointed as members. This Committee may also invite subject specialists/experts from Universities/IMD/commodity Boards/Research Institutions, SRSAC etc., if deemed necessary. If the AC is satisfied that there is an error of judgement by the by the grievance redressal officer at the Tehsil / Taluk level then it may admit the appeal filed before it. The AC shall record the averments of the appellant as well as all the connected parties, examine the issues raised in the light of the operational guidelines and dispose the matter within 15 days by passing a speaking order and the grievance shall be treated as closed. However, in case if the AC is of the view that the appeal is not admissible, it shall reject the same in writing by recording the reasons thereof. 30.4 State Level Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC): The State/UT shall also constitute a State Level Grievance Redressal Committee for redressal of grievance of Farmers, Banks, Insurance Company, CSC-VLE, CSC eGov, Insurance Intermediaries, District Authority/Department unsettled at the level of the DGRC. This Committee will be headed by the Principal Secretary/Secretary of the Nodal Department, SLBC/Banks, Chief General Manager (CGM) NABARD, Insurance Company and the concerned State Authority/Department shall be appointed as members. This Committee may also invite subject specialists/ experts from Agriculture University/ IMD/ research institutions/commodity Boards/, State Remote Sensing Application Centre, SRSAC, STSU, STAC, concerned MITRs etc., if deemed necessary. 30.5 The grievances which have wider scope of effect impacting a greater number of districts or there is a breach of guidelines by any of the stakeholder or the grievance matter exceeds Rs. 25 Lakh in monetary terms, such matters may be directly raised at the level of the State Level Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC). The Committee will dispose of the grievance within 15 days from the time of receipt of grievance. The decision of the Committee shall be accepted by all the parties. ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

य सहकारी सोसाइटी का मुख् य कायाकारी ऐसी ररजियों की सूचना, इसके उद्भुत होने के एक सप् ताह के भीतर प्राजधकरण को संसूजचत करेगा, िो अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार ररजियों को भरने की कारावाई करेगा । (2) अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार वैकजल्पक ररजियों में जनयुक्ट् त कोई ्‍ यजि अजधिेि अवजध तक ही बोडा का सिस्ट् य रहेगा, िब तक वह बोडा के सिस्ट् य जिसके स्ट् थान पर जनयुक्ट् त हुआ है, रहेगा । 19य. मतिान की गोपनीयता का अनुरिण - प्रत् येक अजधकारी, जलजपक, अजभकताा या अन्द् य ्‍ यजि िो दकसी जनवााचन में अजभलेखन या मतगणना से िुड़ा काया जनष् पािन कर रहा है, मतगणना की गोपनीयता अनुरजित करेगा और अनुरिण करने में मिि करेगा और दकसी अन्द् य ्‍ यजि को (जसवाए कुछ प्रयोिनों के जलए दकसी जवजध द्वारा या उसके अधीन प्राजधकृत) ऐसी गोपनीयता का उल् लंघन करने के जलए मतिान से संबंजधत कोई सूचना संप्रेजित नहीं करेगा ।” 5. मूल जनयमों में, जनयम 20 के स्ट् थान पर जनम् नजलजखत जनयम रखे िाएंगे, अथाातम: -

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

ऐसे अभ् यथी जिसका नामांकन स्ट् वीकार दकया गया था, जनवााचन रे होने के पश् चातम ऐसे अभ् यथी की अभ् यर्थाता वापस लेने के नए नोरटस को स्ट् वीकार नहीं दकया िाएगा । 19ध. मतिान के जलए इलेक्ट् रॉजनक मतिान मिीनों तैयार करना - यदि प्राजधकरण मतिान के जलए इलेक्ट् रॉजनक मिीन का उपयोग करने का जनणाय लेता है तो वह इसकी प्रदक्रया जनिेजित करेगा िो िहां तक तकनीकी ूप प से यथािक्ट् य हो, इन जनयमों के अनुसार होगी । 19न. जनवााचन ्‍ यय – जनवााचन संबंधी सभी ्‍ यय जिसमें लेखन सामग्री, मुरण, डाक, फोटोकॉपी, फैक्ट् स, मत पेटी का दकराया, अजमट स्ट् याही, पुजलस सुरिा और अन्द् य ऐसे ्‍ यय की वस्ट् तुओं पर होने वाले ्‍ यय िो बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के प्रजतजनजधयों या जनिेिकों के जनवााचन से संबंजधत है, िैसे मतिाता सूची की तैयारी, यात्रा और अन्द्य भत्ते, और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, सहायक ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, और अन्द्य मतिान कर्मायों को िेय पाररश्रजमक का वहन सोसाइटी द्वारा दकया िाएगा और प्राजधकरण के जनिेि पर प्राजधकरण को भुगतान दकया िाएगा । 19प. जनवााचन ्‍ यय का लेखा - (1) जनवााचन का प्रत् येक अभ् यथी जनवााचन कराने के आिेि की तारीख से उसके पररणाम की घोिणा की तारीख, िोनों तारीख सजम्मजलत, तक जनवााचन से संबंजधत उसके द्वारा या उसके प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि द्वारा दकए गए सभी ्‍ ययों का एक पृथक और सही लेखा पररणाम की घोिणा की तारीख से तीस दिनों की अवजध तक रखेगा । (2) इन लेखों में ऐसी जवजिजियां सजम्मजलत होंगी िो जनयम 19ब में जनर्िाष् ट जववरणों के अजतररक्ट् त समय-समय पर जवजनर्िाष् ट दकए िाएंगे । (3) उक्ट् त ्‍ यय की कुल रकम, प्राजधकरण द्वारा समय-समय पर जवजनर्िाष् ट की गई कुल रकम से अजधक नहीं होगी । (4) जनवााचन लड़ने वाला प्रत् येक अभ् यथी ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के पास अपने जनवााचन ्‍ यय के लेखा को प्राजधकरण द्वारा समय-समय पर जनर्िाष् ट रीजत और समय पर प्रस्ट् तुत करेगा ।

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

3 Financial Literacy - Guidance note for trainers 1. The objective of conduct of financial literacy camps is to facilitate financial inclusion through provision of two essentials i.e. literacy and easy access. It should aim at imparting knowledge to enable financial planning, inculcate saving habits and improve the understanding of financial products leading to effective use of financial services by the common man. Financial literacy should help them plan ahead of time for their life cycle needs and deal with unexpected emergencies without resorting to debt. They should be able to proactively manage money and avoid debt traps. In order to ensure that the knowledge provided through awareness results in inculcating banking habits, literacy inputs need to be synchronized with access to financial services so as to enable the common man to use the information effectively to gain control over financial matters. It should also result in enhancement of their economic security aided by use of banking services. 2. The banks as providers of financial services, have an inherent gain in the spread of financial inclusion and financial literacy, as it would help them capture the untapped business opportunities. Small customer is the key and banks should harness the business opportunities available at the bottom of the pyramid. Hence banks must view the financial literacy efforts as their future investments. Banks must provide a bouquet of banking services comprising of a small overdraft facility, variable recurring deposit account, KCC, remittance facilities to the account holders in order to make the accounts transactional. People should be encouraged to make transactions in these accounts so that the cost of maintaining the accounts is recovered to make it a viable and profitable business of the banks. The provision of adequate credit is also important not only in the interest of the customer, but also for the banks as the income earned through interest earned would make the exercise a commercially viable proposition. Banks must provide credit at a competitive though non exploitative rate but certainly not at a subsidised rate. 3. Creating awareness and knowledge about various products and providing these products at their doorstep would be the first step in capturing the accounts. The objective of Financial Literacy Guide is to create awareness and educate masses in a lucid manner about management of money, importance of savings, advantages of saving with banks, other facilities provided by banks and benefits of borrowing from banks. This guide is a ready reckoner for trainers involved in Financial Literacy and Financial Inclusion. It should be used

2 3. Keeping in view of the extent of exclusion, banks need to conduct these Financial Literacy Camps in a mission mode, with the ultimate objective of making financial inclusion a viable business model by capturing the untapped business opportunities. In accordance with the objectives as stated above, it is necessary to evaluate the effectiveness of financial literacy efforts in linking the excluded segment to the banking system. SLBCs/DCC would review the financial literacy efforts undertaken by FLCs and rural branches under their jurisdiction, as a regular agenda item in the SLBC/DCC meetings. The details of FLCs along with contact details should be published on the respective SLBC website. Similarly Banks’ Head Offices would review the effectiveness of financial literacy efforts undertaken by their FLCs and rural branches. A structured monitoring mechanism both for FLCs and rural branches would be put in place shortly. 4. Banks’ Top Management including CMDs should ensure that all the rural branches and FLCs prepare a calendar for conduct of Financial Literacy Camps in the beginning of the year. They should give wide publicity to the financial literacy drive by attending some of the Financial Literacy Camps conducted by rural branches and FLCs during their outreach visits. In order to ensure consistency in the messages reaching the target audience of financially excluded people during the Financial Literacy Camps, it is necessary for banks to use the Financial Literacy Guide as a standard curriculum to impart basic conceptual understanding of financial products and services. They may also consider converting the contents of this guide into plays, skits, videos, films etc, for use in the Financial Literacy Camps. If necessary, they may get the material published in vernacular languages as well, in consultation with us. For any further details, we may be contacted by email. 5 Conduct of Financial Literacy Camps- Operational Guidelines All the Financial Literacy Centres and rural branches should prepare an annual calendar of locations for conduct of outdoor Financial Literacy Camps. At every location, the program should be conducted in three stages to be spread over a period of three months comprising of three sessions of minimum two hours each plus a visit to ensure timely delivery of cards. Suitable premises or open place for conduct of program should be identified in advance. Banks may customize the program depending upon the requirement of a particular location and available resources. In all circumstances, the underlying objective of the conduct of program should be to bring the maximum number of participants into the banking fold. First Session  The first session would mainly focus on creating awareness on financial concepts, personal finance and management of money amongst the people. For this purpose, bank should organize a camp for a group of villagers. Advance publicity should be given in the village about the conduct of the camp to ensure good attendance by the villagers.  The work of organizing the camp should be taken up beforehand with the involvement of prominent persons of the area like village sarpanch, school teachers or any other person having good rapport with the villagers. Suitable arrangements may be made at the place identified for the conduct of the program. All the charts and play cards should be placed before the arrival of the participants.  Prepare a list of participants with details of name, age, occupation etc.  Topics to be covered should be financial planning, budgeting, savings, how to maintain financial diary, advantages of saving with banks, the concept of a Business Correspondent, difference between formal and informal sources of borrowing, purpose and cost of borrowing, different types of borrowing etc, as given in the guide.  Distribute a financial diary to each of the participants. Explain how to use the financial diary for preparing the budget and maintaining periodical accounts. Reiterate the advantages of maintaining the diary. Ask them to use diary at home for preparing their budget and writing income and expenses for one month. Advise them to bring the diary when they come for the next session.

This will also assist in identification of farmers who have not been enrolled under PMFBY despite they not opting out of the scheme and therefore help in fixing responsibilities on the erring banks and branches for knowingly depriving the farmers from the benefits of the scheme. 39.4.29 Integration with Various Digital Platforms To streamline the ﬂow of information amongst stakeholders, the portal will also be integrated with the system/data being developed by multiple other platforms and digital public infrastructure: a) Settlement of Yield data disputes or disputes relating to crop loss. b) ACF (Area Correction Factor) for insured crop for every season. c) Satellite data-based Clustering. d) Integration of smart sampling tool for CCE plot selection. e) Integration of innovative technology driven approach for rationalization of CCE. f) Integration with the technique that is being developed for estimation of crop yield at Gram Panchayat level. g) Cadastral level crop and land ownership veriﬁcation. h) Smart Sampling technique. i) Agristack and Agri DSS being developed by GoI for the purpose of various data validation and standardization protocols.

The project received inputs from 53 stakeholders, showcasing a collaborative effort to shape the National Cooperative Database. Based on inputs received, sector specific data fields and online forms were developed. Hon’ble Minister of Cooperation accorded in principle approval of the project during a presentation made before him on 30th September 2022. 2.5 National Cooperative Union of India’s contribution in the development of National Cooperative Database: Earlier National Cooperatives Union of India updated state and sector-wise cooperative data on a regular basis for the publication of its Indian Cooperative Movement-Statistical Profile. After the Ministry of Cooperation decided to create a National Cooperative Database on cooperatives, NCUI actively collaborated with the Ministry of Cooperation to develop the National Cooperative Database (NCD). Leveraging its expertise, NCUI's National Cooperative Databank Division (NCDD) plays a vital role in formulating data collection templates and providing insights for efficient data gathering, and supports the National Database Team by contributing to drafting chapters and compiling data for the NCD report. NCUI facilitate the process by creating user IDs for Nodal Officers and Interns/DEOs engaged in data entry and also ensures timely payment of stipends/honorariums of the Interns/DEO(s) and Nodal officers engaged for the data entry of the societies in the NCD portal. NCUI provides invaluable support from the very inception of the NCD project, right through to its successful completion. 2.6 Organizational Structure for Developing Database: The overall work is being carried under the guidance of Secretary (Cooperation). Following operational structure has been put in place; • Steering Committee under Chairmanship of Additional Secretary (Coop) & CRCS was constituted for monitoring of progress and implementation of strategy for development of National Cooperative Database. The members of the Committee is from MoC, PMG, NCDC (LINAC), NCUI & AICTE. • Advisory Committee under Chairmanship of Additional Secretary (Coop) & CRCS was constituted for getting inputs from various stakeholders such as State RCS, National Cooperative Federations and Statutory Bodies (NABARD, NDDB, NFDB). • Project Management Group (PMG) was set up under Chief Project Officer and Ex-DDG (NIC) who is responsible for architecting the portal for National Cooperative Database. PMG has designed and developed the software solution and has been spearheading its implementation across states. Regular meetings of Steering/Advisory Committees and PMG were held to sort out technical & administrative issues, on priority basis, at every stage of database development. Secretary (Cooperation) also reviewed the progress regularly and held frequent meetings with State RCs, National Cooperative Federations & Steering Committee. 2.7 Activities and Funding of Project • Development of sector-specific Web Forms by software development team for collecting data from Primary to Apex cooperative society. • Exhaustive repeated training for Data Entry Operators (DEOs) and Nodal Officers at district level. • Collection of data from District Registrar Offices of State RCS and

26 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report in different sectors through interns/ DEOs. • Verification and correction of each and every record for all field officials. A module was developed wherein the district nodal officers submitted certificates on completion of verified entries. • Cross validation of data from State RCS, St.CB, DCCB, NABARD, NDDB, NFDB, NAFSCOB, NCDFI & FISHCOFED. • Documentation of software application and technical flows, Standardization of Master code, user manual and training manual. • Development of Analytical Dashboard, MIS Reports, Graphical Presentations, GIS Maps to show coverage under various Cooperatives, Query Based Reports and Multiple Level of User Access through User Management Module. • The expenditure on procuring hardware & software, engaging IT Professional & Interns/DEOs, etc. for National Cooperative Database has been met through Cooperative Education Fund (CEF). 2.8 Data Collection for Database in Phased Manner Keeping in view the diverse nature and size of cooperative sector, it was decided to create the database in a phased manner. Phase-I: Under Phase-I, mapping of about 2.64 lakh primary cooperative societies of three sectors i.e., Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS), Dairy and Fisheries was completed in February, 2023. Under this phase, in addition to staff at district registrar offices services of 560 local interns enrolled on portal of All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) were onboarded for data entries at District Registrar Offices. Phase-II: Under this Phase, Mapping of National Cooperative Societies/Federations along with their General Body Members was completed. Further, their downward linkages with State Federations, District Unions and Primary Cooperative were also established. The data related to StCB, DCCB, UCB, SCARDB, PCARDB, Sugar Cooperative Mills, State Federations, District Unions and MSCS were collected directly from cooperative societies or through their National/State Federations. Phase-III: Under this Phase, Ministry of Cooperation initiated the process of extending the National Cooperative Database to remaining more than 5 lakh cooperative societies working in all other sectors, through the office of RCSs of State/UTs. Almost all States/UTs have completed data entry under National Cooperative Database. By November 2023, the data of around 8 lakh primary cooperative societies has been uploaded on the National Cooperative Database by the nodal officers of States/UTs. The total number of members engaged in these cooperative societies are around 29,12,80,275. 2.9 Linkage with other Databases A central project has been formulated for the automation of cooperative registration and management processes in the offices of the Registrar of Cooperative Society of States/ UTs. The process has been initiated to have API-based linkages of the software system that is being developed for use at state and district-level registrar offices with the National Cooperative Database (NCD). This will ensure the real-time updating of data on the National Cooperative Database about registration of any new cooperative society as well as updation of other data items in respect of existing cooperative societies. NCD, being centralized platform of all sectors of cooperatives, depending on the sectoral parameters, it is important to create live linkages with other databases of central departments and state

assets and liabilities, etc. It involved development of a web based secure system to facilitate data feeding from each of the district registrar/functional registrar office which can be viewed and verified by respective state registrar office. By adopting latest IT Tools and Management Information System (MIS), NCD is available on real-time basis to all stakeholders and can easily be adopted for various activities over a period of time.

results.retrieved_text: 56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members.
