35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

5 NATIONAL COOPERATION POLICY 2025 1. Introduction 1.1. A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons, united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly owned and democratically member-controlled enterprise. 1.2. India has more than 8 lakh cooperative societies, comprising around 2 lakh credit cooperatives and 6 lakh non-credit cooperatives. Non- credit cooperatives primarily operate in sectors such as housing, dairy, labour, and others, including sugar, consumer, marketing, fisheries, textiles, services, processing, hospitals, etc. Moreover, with about 30 crore total members in the cooperative sector, PACS alone have more than 13 crore members spread across the country. 1.3. The last policy on cooperatives, released in 2002, focused on the basic dimensions of efficiently organizing economic activities by cooperatives. Over the last 20 years, the world has witnessed radical changes at individual, societal, national, and global levels. They have been driven by globalization and technological advancements, especially in communications and information technology. Given these developments, it became essential to revisit the policy and formulate a new one to suit the evolving requirements of the cooperative sector and to ensure the sustainability of this sector in the current economic scenario. 1.4. Recognizing the formation of cooperative societies as a fundamental right under the Constitution of India and the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation marked a new era. This era requires transformation of the cooperative movement with “farmers, women and rural development” at its centre, along with strengthening cooperative societies, making national federations lead the way, and ensuring both Central and State Governments provide the needed support and recognition for these institutions to grow. Hence, there is an urgent need for a new national policy. 1.5. The vision of ‘Sahkar-Se-Samriddhi’ as articulated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India gives an endearing message motivating the stakeholders and instilling confidence in the sector. It has motivated the Ministry and the cooperative sector to work together towards achieving the above vision.

DEFINITION OF A COOPERATIVE A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly-owned and democratically-controlled enterprise. COOPERATIVE VALUES Cooperatives are based on the values of self-help, self-responsibility, democracy, equality, equity, and solidarity. In the tradition of their founders, cooperative members believe in the ethical values of honesty, openness, social responsibility and caring for others. COOPERATIVE PRINCIPLES The cooperative principles are guidelines by which cooperatives put their values into practice. 1. Voluntary and Open Membership Cooperatives are voluntary organisations, open to all persons able to use their services and willing to accept the responsibilities of membership, without gender, social, racial, political or religious discrimination. 2. Democratic Member Control Cooperatives are democratic organisations controlled by their members, who actively participate in setting their policies and making decisions. Men and women serving as elected representatives are accountable to the membership. In primary cooperatives members have equal voting rights (one member, one vote) and cooperatives at other levels are also organised in a democratic manner. 3. Member Economic Participation Members contribute equitably to, and democratically control, the capital of their cooperative. At least part of that capital is usually the common property of the cooperative. Members usually receive limited compensation, if any, on capital subscribed as a condition of membership. Members allocate surpluses for any or all of the following purposes: developing their cooperative, possibly by setting up reserves, part of which at least would be indivisible, benefiting members in proportion to their transactions with the cooperative, and supporting other activities approved by the membership. 4. Autonomy and Independence Cooperatives are autonomous, self-help organisations controlled by their members. If they enter into agreements with other organisations, including governments, or raise capital from external sources, they do so on terms that ensure democratic control by their members and maintain their cooperative autonomy. 5. Education, Training, and Information Cooperatives provide education and training for their members, elected representatives, managers, end employees so they can contribute effectively to the development of their cooperatives. They inform the general public - particularly young people and opinion leaders about the nature and benefits of co- operation. 6. Cooperation among Cooperatives Cooperatives serve their members most effectively and strengthen the cooperative movement by working together through local, national, regional and international structures. 7. Concern for Community Cooperatives work for the sustainable development of their communities through policies approved by their members.

49 Sector-wise Cooperatives L ong-term rural credit cooperatives were established for providing funds for investment in agriculture – including land development, farm mechanisation and minor irrigation - rural industries and housing. This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The financial health of PCARDBs is, however, more fragile than SCARDBs, given the high share of accumulated losses on their balance sheets. A2. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. # Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) ## Basic Information **Official Name:** Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) **Common Name:** PACS **Type:** Grassroots cooperative credit society **Sector:** Agriculture, rural credit and cooperative development **Primary Role:** PACS are the grassroots level institutions of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCC). Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. 36 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report P rimary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) constitute the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) in the country, primarily providing short-term and medium-term credit facility and other input services, like seed, fertilizer, pesticide distribution, etc. to member farmers. PACS are refinanced by NABARD through District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs). Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Significantly, the growth of PACS has been substantial, expanding from approximately 2,982 PACS in 1900-1923 to 14,391 PACS in 2011-2023. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Kerala boasts the highest number of members (2,56,28,261), trailed by Bihar (1,36,29,113) and Tamil Nadu (1,33,39,395). Around 78% PACS (78,489) are affiliated with Federations/ Unions. Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. Importantly, strengthening PACS involves enhancing their capacity and effectiveness to provide a spectrum of services to farmers and rural communities beyond credit and financial services. Governments and stakeholders aim to uplift rural communities, improve the overall state of agriculture, and foster inclusive economic growth by reinforcing PACS. These efforts will contribute towards reducing poverty, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in agrarian economies. A1. 56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

यजि के वेतन और भत्ते से ऐसी पेंिन की कुल राजि, यदि कोई हो, को घटाकर उसके द्वारा आहरण या आहररत दकया िाएगा । (5) ऑम् बुड्समसमैन द्वारा िौरे पर या स्ट् थानांतरण पर (कायाभार ग्रहण करने के जलए या उसके कायाकाल की समाजप्त पर गृहनगर िाने के जलए की गई यात्रा सजहत) उसके यात्रा भत्ता, िैजनक भत्ते, जनिी सामान के पररवहन और अन्द् य समान मामलों की हकिारी भारत सरकार के जनिेिक के जलए लागू समान वेतनमान और समान िर पर होगी ।

CHAPTER II CENTRAL REGISTRAR AND REGISTRATION OF MULTI-STATE CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES 4. Central Registrar.—(1) The Central Government may appoint a person to be the Central Registrar of Co-operative Societies and may appoint such other persons as it may think fit to assist the Central Registrar. (2) The Central Government may, by notification, direct that any power exercisable by the Central Registrar under this Act (other than the power of registration of a multi-State co-operative society) shall, in relation to such society, and such matters as may be specified in the notification, be exercisable also by any other officer of the Central Government or of a State Government as may be authorised by the Central Government subject to such conditions as may be specified therein: Provided that no officer of a State Government shall be empowered to exercise such power in relation to a national co-operative society. 5. Multi-State co-operative societies which may be registered.—(1) No multi-State co-operative society shall be registered under this Act, unless,— (a) its main objects are to serve the interests of members in more than one state; and (b) its bye-laws provide for social and economic betterment of its members through self-help and mutual aid in accordance with the co-operative principles. (2) The word “limited” or its equivalent in any Indian language shall be suffixed to the name of every multi-State co-operative society registered under this Act with limited liability. 6. Application for registration.—(1) For the purposes of registration of a multi-State co-operative society under this Act, an application shall be made to the Central Registrar in such form and with such particulars as may be prescribed. (2) The application shall be signed,— (a) in the case of a multi-State co-operative society of which all the members are individuals, by at least fifty persons from each of the state concerned; (b) in the case of a multi-State co-operative society of which the members are co-operative societies, by duly authorised representatives on behalf of at least five such societies as are not registered in the same State; and (c) in the case of a multi-State co-operative society of which another multi-State co-operative society and other co-operative societies are members, by duly authorised representatives of each of such societies: Provided that not less than two of the co-operative societies referred to in this clause, shall be such as are not registered in the same State; (d) in the case of a multi-State co-operative society of which the members are co-operative societies or multi-State co-operative societies and individuals, by at least— (i) fifty persons, being individuals, from each of the two States or more; and (ii) one co-operative society each from two States or more or one multi-State co-operative society. 56 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report U rban Cooperative Banks are primarily localised financial service providers that have been in operation for more than a century. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।
iv

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

[भाग II—खण् ड 3(i)] भारत का रािपत्र : असाधारण 9 अजधकारी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संतुष् ट होता है और मतिान केंर में उपजस्ट्थत दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा से कोई आपजत्त नहीं होती है, तो वह मतपत्र पर ही जछदरत अधपन्द् ने पर उक्ट् त सिस्ट् य या प्रजतजनजध का हस्ट् तािर या अंगु े की छाप लेकर उसे मत पत्र िारी करेगा और अधपन्द् ने पर मतपत्र का क्रमांक और अन्द् य जववरण होगा तथा मतपत्र प्राप् त करने के बाि, सिस्ट् य पृथक स्ट् थाजपत मतिान कंपाटामेंट िाएगा और पूरी गोपनीयता के साथ अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों, िो भी ििा हो, के नाम के आगे जिसे वह अपना मत िेना चाहता है, ‘X’ का जचह्न लगाकर अपने मताजधकार का प्रयोग करके मतपत्र को इस प्रयोिन हेतु रखी मतपेटी में डालेगा । परंतु दक िृजिहीनता या अन्द् य िारीररक दि्‍ यांगता या जनरिरता के कारण यदि कोई सिस्ट् य मतपत्र पर जनिान लगाने में असमथा है तो मतिान अजधकारी, और िहां ऐसे मतिान अजधकारी जनयुक्ट् त नहीं हैं, वहां ररटर्नंग अजधकारी उससे अभ् यथी या अभ् यर्थायों का नाम सुजनजश्चत करेगा जिसके पि में वह अपना मत िेने को इच् छुक है और उसकी ओर से ‘X’ का जनिान लगाकर मतपत्र को मतपेटी में डालेगा । (8) प्रत् येक सिस्ट् य जिसका नाम मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों/प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची में प्रजवष् ट है, जिसे मतिान अजधकारी को सुपुिा दकया गया है, को अपना मतिान करने का हक है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को संिर्भात करेगा िो एक संजिप् त िांच करके सोसाइटी के ररकॉडा के संिभा में आपजत्त पर जनणाय करेगा । (9) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके मतिान अजभकताा द्वारा दकसी सिस्ट् य की पहचान से संबंजधत दकसी आपजत्त पर तब तक जवचार नहीं करेगा िब तक दक आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजि ने प्रत् येक ऐसे मत के जलए 5/- रुपए की फीस का संिाय न कर दिया हो और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी तत् पश् चातम आपजत्त पर जवचार करेगा और मतिान करने आए सिस्ट् य से उसके अंगु े की छाप या हस्ट् तािर, िो भी ििा हो, उसकी पहचान का वणान करने वाली उघोषोिणा पर लेगा और यदि वह ऐसा करने से इंकार करता है तो उसे मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी और यदि िूसरी ओर, ऐसी संजिप् त छानबीन पर ररटर्नंग अजधकारी की संतुजि के अनुसार सिस्ट् य की पहचान स्ट् थाजपत हो िाती है तो मतिान अजधकारी मतपत्र िारी करेगा और सिस्ट् य को तब मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार

पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

(4) The Returning Officer shall, at the close of the time fixed for the receipt of nomination Forms, prepare and display on the notice board of the society, a list of nominations received by him and any nomination Form submitted after the date and time fixed for its receipt, shall be rejected. (5) No person shall be nominated as a candidate for election to fill a seat on the board if he— (a) is ineligible to vote; (b) is not qualified or is disqualified to be the member of a multi-State co-operative society or a member of the board under the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder; and (c) does not possess the necessary qualifications specified in the bye-laws of the society for election as member of the board. 19K. Compliance with sections 43 and 44 of the Act.— The eligibility of the candidates for the election of members of the board and office bearers shall be subject to the provisions contained in sections 43 and 44 of the Act. 19L. Scrutiny of nomination papers.—(1) On the day fixed for the scrutiny of nomination papers,— (a) the Returning Officer shall, at the appointed hours, take up the scrutiny of nomination Forms and the candidate or the proposer or seconder of each of the candidates may be present at the time and place when nomination papers are scrutinised; (b) the Returning Officer shall examine the nomination Forms and shall decide all objections which may be made by any candidate or his proposer or seconder in respect of any nomination and may, either accept or reject any nomination: Provided that the nomination of a candidate shall not be rejected on the ground of an incorrect description of his name or the name of his proposer or seconder or of any other particulars relating to the candidate or his proposer or seconder, as entered in the list of members; if the identity of the candidate, proposer or seconder, as the case may be, is established beyond reasonable doubt; (c) the Returning Officer shall endorse on each nomination Form his decision of accepting or rejecting the same, as the case may be, and if the nomination paper is rejected, he shall record in writing a brief statement of his reasons for such rejection; (d) the Returning Officer shall not allow any adjournment of the proceedings except when proceedings are interrupted or obstructed by a riot or affray or by any other cause beyond his control; and (e) list of valid nominations accepted by the Returning Officer shall be published on the notice board of the society containing the names in the alphabetical order in English and address of the candidates as given in the nomination paper. The term Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), though not formally defined, refers to primary cooperative banks located in urban and semi-urban areas. UCBs are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Ministry of Cooperation, in coordination with the Reserve Bank, has initiated reforms to strengthen the cooperative banking structure. The vision guiding the framework is to consolidate their position as friendly neighbourhood banks by catering to the heterogeneity in the customer base, while offering more operational flexibility to strong UCBs in order to enhance their contribution to credit intermediation Over a period of 120 years of their existence, Urban Cooperative Banks are successfully serving the society and meeting banking needs of their customers and members. Being local banks, they are the preferred friendly “Neighbourhood banks of Choice” as they provide doorstep banking services to their customers. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records 1,335 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Around 63% of these banks are located in 3 states namely Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. The State of Maharashtra tops the list with 428 banks having 60,21,811 members, followed by Karnataka (279) having 23,35,863 members and Gujarat (187) having 14,91,531 members. In view of their importance in providing credit to the poor and weaker sections of the society, the RBI is giving focused attention for strengthening the sector. The Hon’ble Minister of Home and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has given a vision to have one UCB in each town of India, so that these UCBs can meet growing credit needs of MSMEs and help in economic growth of the country. 4.7 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

43 Sector-wise Cooperatives T he cooperative movement in our country can be traced to ancient India and the Cooperative Banks, as we know of them today, are more than a century old. These banks were one of the first sources of institutional credit to the farmers in our country. Banks are unique in the sense that their functioning is inherently driven by values viz. equality, open and voluntary association, democracy, mutual support, self-reliance, non- exploitative operations etc. which are mostly absent in other forms of credit institutions. District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) stand at the second tier in the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS) having State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) at the State/ Apex level and Primary Agriculture Credit Cooperative Societies (PACS) at the village level. DCCBs come under the regulatory purview of RBI through Banking Regulation, Act, 1949 (AACS). As per National Cooperative Database, there are 338 District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) functioning across 19 States/UTs. 4.2 District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs)

35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. Being the grassroots level cooperative institutions, PACS play a crucial role in sustaining the rural economy of the country by purveying institutional credit to small and marginal farmers. PACS are governed by the Cooperative Acts of their respective states and guided by State Bye-laws. They engage directly with rural (agricultural) borrowers, extending loans, overseeing loan repayments, and managing marketing and distribution functions. Notably, the National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal records the presence of 1,03,304 PACS in the country, with around 95% (i.e., 98,486) of them are being functional in rural areas. Maharashtra has the highest number of PACS (21,059) followed by Gujarat (10,266) and Bihar (8,476). Out of total 2,69,503 gram panchayats, around 89% (i.e., 2,41,075) panchayats are covered under PACS. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. To bring in efficiency, accountability, transparency at PACS and improve profitability. b. To bring in accuracy and uniformity in the conduct of business, accounting with

This structure consists of 14 State Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (SCARDBs) operating at the state level and 533 Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) operating at the district/ block level. The structure of long-term rural credit cooperatives differs across states. States like Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Puducherry follow a unitary structure i.e., SCARDBs operate through their own branches with no separate PCARDBs. On the other hand, states like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu follow a federal structure wherein SCARDBs lend through PCARDBs. In two states viz., Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal, SCARDBs operate through PCARDBs as well as through their own branches. The business model of SCARDBs and PCARDBs depends heavily on borrowings; the former borrow from institutions such as NABARD for direct lending as well as lending through PCARDBs. The mission places particular emphasis on: * Rural women * Poor rural households * Members of eligible Self-Help Groups * Vulnerable households * Rural entrepreneurs * Eligible rural youth under relevant components Final eligibility depends on the applicable programme and State implementation guidelines. ## Role of Self-Help Groups SHGs are an important institutional platform under DAY-NRLM. They help members collectively: * Save * Borrow * Plan livelihood activities * Access financial services * Develop enterprises * Improve income opportunities * Connect with government programmes and markets ## Application / Access DAY-NRLM is implemented through State Rural Livelihoods Missions and local community institutions. Rural households interested in accessing DAY-NRLM support can approach: * Self-Help Groups * Village-level organizations * Gram Panchayat * Block-level rural livelihood mission office * State Rural Livelihoods Mission * District Rural Development authorities * Other designated implementing agencies The exact process varies by State and programme component. ## Documents / Information Depending on the programme component, applicants or SHG members may need: * Household details * Identity information * Bank account details * SHG membership information * Mobile number * Livelihood or enterprise details * Project or business plan where applicable * Other information required by the implementing authority Exact document requirements vary according to the State and programme component. ## Implementation DAY-NRLM is implemented through a multi-level institutional structure involving: * Ministry of Rural Development * State Rural Livelihoods Missions * District-level agencies * Block-level teams * Community institutions * Self-Help Groups Community participation is an important part of programme implementation. ## Frequently Asked Questions / Intents ### What is DAY-NRLM? DAY-NRLM is a rural livelihoods mission of the Government of India that aims to reduce rural poverty by supporting livelihoods, Self-Help Groups, financial inclusion, skills and rural enterprises. ### What does DAY-NRLM stand for? DAY-NRLM stands for Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission. ### Who benefits from DAY-NRLM? The mission primarily focuses on poor and vulnerable rural households, especially rural women organized into Self-Help Groups. ### What is the role of SHGs under DAY-NRLM? SHGs help rural women collectively save, access credit, undertake livelihood activities, develop enterprises and access financial and government services. ### Does DAY-NRLM provide financial support? Depending on the applicable component, DAY-NRLM can facilitate financial inclusion, access to credit and other forms of support for eligible SHGs and rural households. ### Can women join an SHG under DAY-NRLM? Eligible rural women can participate in Self-Help Groups formed and supported through the rural livelihoods mission. ### Does DAY-NRLM support rural businesses? Yes. Applicable components can support rural enterprises, entrepreneurship, training, technical assistance and market linkages. ### Does DAY-NRLM support agriculture and dairy activities? Yes. Livelihood support can include agriculture, livestock, dairy, fisheries and other activities depending on State programmes and applicable guidelines. ###

45 Sector-wise Cooperatives A State’s three-tier rural cooperative credit structure consists of State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), and Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), which concentrate on agricultural and rural development. State cooperative banks are the apex institutions in this structure. The National Cooperative Database (NCD) records the presence of 32 registered State Cooperative Banks in the country except for 5 States/UTs namely Haryana, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, Manipur, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. These cooperative banks offer a comprehensive range of services, from savings accounts to agricultural loans, actively supporting priority sectors and contributing to the well-being of local communities. 52 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report C redit and Thrift Societies are member-driven financial institutions registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of various states in India. They play a very significant role in meeting credit needs of poor and marginalized sections of the society. They offer customized loan products and repayment schedules based on members’ needs and income levels and foster a sense of community and social responsibility among members. In India, there are 79,795 primary credit and thrift societies in 34 States, except for Ladakh and Kerala, with 4.32 crore members. Out of 79,795 societies, 66,713 societies are functional, 10,489 are dormant and 2,593 are under liquidation. Around 56% societies i.e., 44,404 are operating in urban areas and the remaining 35,391 societies are operating in rural areas. Telangana and Maharashtra have the maximum number of credit and thrift societies. Approximately 55% of the total primary credit and thrift societies are operating in these two states alone. The remaining 45% of the societies are operating in 32 states. Telangana state has the highest number of societies i.e., 24,020 with a membership base of 47.77 lakh followed by Maharashtra which has 20,337 societies with 2.27 crore members. The core functions of these societies are: • Thrift: Encouraging members to save regularly through deposits, often with attractive interest rates compared to traditional savings accounts. • Credit: Providing loans to members for various purposes like education, medical expenses, business ventures, or agricultural needs, often at lower interest rates than commercial banks. • Other Services: Many societies offer additional services like micro-insurance, money transfers, and financial literacy programs. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. 35 Sector-wise Cooperatives Collectives, including cooperatives, mandate their members to pool in surplus money for onward lending to borrower members. Some of these adhere to the principle of self-help where the products and services are used entirely by their members. Emerging collectives, including credit cooperatives, carry out bulk of their business with non-members. Credit Cooperatives – both banks and credit societies–are the lifeline for all economic activities of members. A strong urban and rural cooperative banking and credit sector can play a catalytic role for growth of cooperatives in various segments of economy. Cooperative banks are basically cooperative societies which are registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of the State concerned or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. Rural long-term credits are disbursed through SCARDBs and PCARDBs. A. Credit Sector Sector-wise Cooperatives

52 National Cooperative Database 2023 : A Report C redit and Thrift Societies are member-driven financial institutions registered under the Cooperative Societies Act of various states in India. They play a very significant role in meeting credit needs of poor and marginalized sections of the society. They offer customized loan products and repayment schedules based on members’ needs and income levels and foster a sense of community and social responsibility among members. In India, there are 79,795 primary credit and thrift societies in 34 States, except for Ladakh and Kerala, with 4.32 crore members. Out of 79,795 societies, 66,713 societies are functional, 10,489 are dormant and 2,593 are under liquidation. Around 56% societies i.e., 44,404 are operating in urban areas and the remaining 35,391 societies are operating in rural areas. Telangana and Maharashtra have the maximum number of credit and thrift societies. Approximately 55% of the total primary credit and thrift societies are operating in these two states alone. The remaining 45% of the societies are operating in 32 states. Telangana state has the highest number of societies i.e., 24,020 with a membership base of 47.77 lakh followed by Maharashtra which has 20,337 societies with 2.27 crore members. The core functions of these societies are: • Thrift: Encouraging members to save regularly through deposits, often with attractive interest rates compared to traditional savings accounts. • Credit: Providing loans to members for various purposes like education, medical expenses, business ventures, or agricultural needs, often at lower interest rates than commercial banks. • Other Services: Many societies offer additional services like micro-insurance, money transfers, and financial literacy programs. Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) are village- or panchayat-level cooperative societies that form the lowest tier of the Short-Term Cooperative Credit Structure. PACS deal directly with rural and agricultural borrowers. They provide loans, collect repayment of loans, and may undertake distribution and marketing functions. PACS are an important link between farmers and the higher levels of the cooperative credit system, including District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), State Cooperative Banks (StCBs), and NABARD. --- ## Why are PACS Important? PACS help connect farmers and rural communities with: * Agricultural credit * Farm inputs * Agricultural services * Storage facilities * Markets and distribution * Other cooperative and government-supported services The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS as the grassroots base of the cooperative credit structure. PACS can help bring farmers closer to credit, agricultural inputs, markets and value addition. --- ## What Services Can PACS Provide? Traditional PACS activities include: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term credit * Distribution of seeds * Distribution of fertilizers * Distribution of pesticides * Storage-related services * Agricultural input services * Marketing and distribution functions * Loan repayment and related credit services Under the Model Bye-laws and diversification initiatives, PACS can also undertake multiple activities beyond traditional credit. These may include: * Dairy activities * Fisheries activities * Floriculture * Food-grain procurement * Warehousing and storage * Fair Price Shops * LPG/CNG/Petrol/Diesel distributorship * Common Service Centre (CSC) services * Business Correspondent or banking-related activities * Insurance-related services * Custom Hiring Centres * Other permitted business activities The exact activities available at an individual PACS depend on its applicable State Cooperative Societies Act, bye-laws, permissions and local implementation. --- ## What Types of Loans Does PACS Provide? PACS traditionally provide: * Short-term agricultural credit * Medium-term agricultural credit The Model Bye-laws and computerization framework also cover financial services involving short-, medium- and long-term loans. However, the exact loan products, limits, interest rates, repayment periods and eligibility conditions depend on the applicable cooperative rules, State provisions and the individual PACS or financing structure. While cooperative societies functioning within a single state are governed by Cooperative Societies Act of their respective state, cooperative societies functioning in more than one State/ UT are governed by Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 under the purview of Government of India. When cooperative societies carry on the business of banking, they come under the regulatory purview of RBI and they are licensed under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act. The cooperative banking structure in India was developed to complement and supplement the commercial banking structure, with a specific focus on serving the requirements of marginalised borrowers and meeting the development needs of rural as well as urban areas. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) are classified as scheduled and non-scheduled, based on their inclusion or otherwise in the second schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and their geographical outreach (single-state or multi-state). Rural cooperatives are segregated by their lending activity, i.e., into short-term vis-à-vis long-term lending. Rural credit short-term credits are channelled through StCB, DCCBs and PACS. top3.text: 3 PACS Computerisation Project - Guidelines 1 Introduction The Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) form the vital third tier in the three- tier structure of the Short Term Cooperative Credit Structure (STCCS). The other two tiers are comprised of District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCBs) (2nd tier) and State Cooperative Bank (StCBs) (1st tier). National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has earlier taken the initiative to bring most of the StCBs and DCCBs on Core Banking Solutions (CBS) platform which has enabled them to give modern-day technology-based banking facilities to their clients. However, the PACS have so far been largely out of the ambit of the technology support. PACS are owned by farmers, rural artisans etc. and aim at promoting thrift and mutual help among the members; cater to their credit requirements and provide credit-linked services like input supply, storage and marketing of agricultural produce etc. DCCBs provide direct linkages to the PACS through direct financing. The StCBs are primarily responsible for control and coordination of the finances of DCCBs. The large out-reach of PACS to the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) make them a systemically important class of agricultural credit purveying institutions. Further, there is a felt need to develop cooperatives as vibrant business enterprises by enabling them to provide multiple services to their members with support of technology in order to fulfil members’ requirements. Keeping in view the above and to make PACS self-reliant in tune with ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan’, the Government of India (GoI) has, on 29th June 2022 approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies for a period of five years from 2022-23 to 2026-27. 2 Aims & Objectives of the Project The aims and objectives of the project inter alia include the following: a. मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

है िबतक दक उसकी पहचान के जवरुद्ध अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा द्वारा आपजत्त न हो । यदि दकसी सिस्ट् य के जवरुद्ध ऐसी कोई आपजत्त आती है या यदि मतिान अजधकारी को कोई तकासंगत संिेह को, तो वह मामले को ररटर्नंग और मतिान करने आए सिस्ट् य से उसके अंगु े की छाप या हस्ट् तािर, िो भी ििा हो, उसकी पहचान का वणान करने वाली उघोषोिणा पर लेगा और यदि वह ऐसा करने से इंकार करता है तो उसे मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी और यदि िूसरी ओर, ऐसी संजिप् त छानबीन पर ररटर्नंग अजधकारी की संतुजि के अनुसार सिस्ट् य की पहचान स्ट् थाजपत हो िाती है तो मतिान अजधकारी मतपत्र िारी करेगा और सिस्ट् य को तब मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार

top3.text: पर भी चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस नोरटस में जनम् नजलजखत सूचनाएं होंगी, अथाातम: (क) जनवााचन द्वारा भरी िाने वाली ररजियों की संख् या ; (ख) जनवााचन का िेत्र (उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट) जिसमें से सिस्ट् यों का जनवााचन दकया िाना है ; (ग) बोडा की सिस्ट् यता की पात्रता हेतु उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट अहाताएं, यदि कोई हैं ; (घ) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी का नाम, तारीख, स्ट् थान और समय जिस िौरान सिस्ट् यों द्वारा नामांकन कागज़ भरा िाएगा, वह तारीख िो जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख से न्द् यूनतम स्ट् पष् ट एक दिन पहले हो या यदि वह एक अवकाि का दिन है तो उससे पूवावती दिन िो सावािजनक अवकाि न हो । स्ट् पष् टीकरण- इस जनयम के प्रयोिन से िब् ि ‘सावािजनक अवकाि’ से ऐसा कोई दिन अजभप्रेत है िो परक्राम् य जलखत अजधजनयम, 1981 (1881 का 26) की धारा 25 के अधीन या ऐसा कोई दिन िो केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार द्वारा, िो भी ििा हो, केन्द् रीय सरकार या राज् य सरकार के कायाालयों के जलए, िो भी ििा हो, सावािजनक अवकाि के ूपप में अजधसूजचत की गई हो ; (ङ) वह तारीख और वह समय और स्ट् थान िब नामांकन कागिों की िांच की िाएगी; और (च) वह तारीख और समय तथा वह स्ट् थान और समय िब मतिान होगा । 19-स. सिस्ट् यों और प्रजतजनजधयों की सूची को तैयार करना - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा उस तारीख के अनुसार िो मतिान के जलए जनयत तारीख से तीस दिन पूवा मतिान के जलए पात्र सिस्ट् यों की सूची तैयार की िाएगी और सूची की प्रजतजलजपयों को सोसाइटी के कारबार के मूल स्ट् थान और इसकी सभी िाखाओं, यदि कोई हो, के नोरटस बोडा पर जनवााचन हेतु जनयत तारीख के न्द् यूनतम पंरह दिन पूवा चस्ट् पा की िाएगी और इस सूची में जनम् नजलजखत जवजनर्िाष् ट होंगे - (क) सिस्ट् य का िाजखला संख् या और नाम, जपता या पजत का नाम, और व्यजिक की ििा में ऐसे सिस्ट् य का पता; और

मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । ऐसी ििा में भुगतान की गई आपजत्त फीस िब् त कर ली िाएगी । (10) मतिान के अंत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी एकजत्रत आपजत्त फीस, आपजत्त करने वाले ्‍ यजियों को वापस की गई फीस और िब् त की गई फीस का जहसाब तैयार करेगा और साथ में प्रत् येक मामले में संजिप् त िांच के पश् चातम उसके द्वारा जलए गए जनणायों का संजिप् त सार सोसाइटी को िेगा । (11) यदि मतिान के दकसी चरण में, िंगा या हंगामा द्वारा कायावाही अवरुद्ध या बाजधत होती है या यदि ऐसे जनवााचन में दकसी पयााप् त कारणों से मतिान कराना संभव नहीं है तो ररटर्नंग अजधकारी को मतिान रे करने के ऐसे कारणों को अजभलेजखत करने के पश् चातम, मतिान रे करने की िजि होगी । (12) मतिान के जलए जनयत समय के पश् चातम दकसी मतिाता को मतिान करने की अनुमजत नहीं िी िाएगी । परंतु दक यदि कोई मतिाता, मतिान के समय की समाजप्त के पूवा पररसर में प्रवेि कर चुका हो तो उसे मतपत्र िारी कर मतिान करने की अनुमजत िी िाएगी । (13) मतिान की समाजप्त के ीक पश् चातम मतगणना आरंभ की िाएगी और यदि ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जनयंत्रण से परे यदि मतों की गणना तुरंत संभव नहीं है तो मतपेटी को ररटर्नंग अजधकारी और जनवााचन में खड़े अभ् यर्थायों या उनके एिेंटों के मुहरों से मुहरबंि कर दिया िाएगा, और यदि यह उनकी इच् छा हो तो मतपेरटयां सोसाइटी की सुरजित अजभरिा में िमा कर िी िाएगी और ऐसी जस्ट्थजत में ररटर्नंग अजधकारी अगले दिन आरंभ होने वाली मतगणना का स्ट् थान और समय की घोिणा करेगा और अभ् यथी और उसके अजभकतााओं को जलजखत में भी सूजचत करेगा और मतगणना अगले दिन ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या उसके पयावेिण में की िाएगी और प्रत् येक अभ् यथी और उनके प्राजधकृत अजभकताा को मतगणना के समय उपजस्ट्थत रहने का अजधकार होगा तथा दकसी अभ् यथी या उसके अजभकताा के मतगणना में अनुपजस्ट्थत रहने से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना या पररणाम की घोिणा जनष् प्रभावी नहीं होगी । (14) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा मतगणना की समाजप्त के पश् चातम, वह मतिान के पररणाम की एक जववरणी तैयार करेगा और प्राजधकरण के पूवाानुमोिन से तुरंत पररणाम घोजित करेगा ।

ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, उसके द्वारा प्राप् त नामांकनों की सूची तैयार कर सोसाइटी की नोरटस बोडा में प्रिर्िात करेगा और ऐसा कोई नामांकन प्रूपप िो उसकी प्राजप्त के जलए जनयत तारीख और समय पर या उससे पहले प्राप् त नहीं होता है, को रे कर दिया िाएगा । (5) बोडा के ररक्ट् त स्ट् थान को भरने के जलए जनवााचन में ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को अभ् यथी के ूपप में नामांदकत नहीं दकया िाएगा यदि वह - (क) मतिान के जलए अपात्र हो; (ख) अर्हात न हो या अजधजनयम या इन जनयमों के उपबंधों के अधीन दकसी बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में या बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूपप में अयोग् य हराया गया हो; और (ग) बोडा के सिस्ट् य के ूप प में जनवााचन हेतु सोसाइटी की उपजवजधयों में जवजनर्िाष् ट आवश् यक अहाताएं नहीं रखता हो । 19ट. अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 का अनुपालन - बोडा के सिस्ट् य, और पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन के जलए अभ् यर्थायों की पात्रता अजधजनयम की धारा 43 और 44 में जनजहत उपबंधों के अध् याधीन होंगी । 19 . नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन - (1) नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन के जलए जनयत दिन को – (क) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी जनर्िाष् ट समय पर नामांकन पत्र की छानबीन का काया करेगा और अभ् यथी या प्रत् येक अभ् यथी का प्रस्ट् तावक या अनुसमथाक, नामांकन पत्र की िांच के समय उस स्ट् थान पर उपजस्ट्थत रह सकता है ।

यजि के वेतन और भत्ते से ऐसी पेंिन की कुल राजि, यदि कोई हो, को घटाकर उसके द्वारा आहरण या आहररत दकया िाएगा । (5) ऑम् बुड्समसमैन द्वारा िौरे पर या स्ट् थानांतरण पर (कायाभार ग्रहण करने के जलए या उसके कायाकाल की समाजप्त पर गृहनगर िाने के जलए की गई यात्रा सजहत) उसके यात्रा भत्ता, िैजनक भत्ते, जनिी सामान के पररवहन और अन्द् य समान मामलों की हकिारी भारत सरकार के जनिेिक के जलए लागू समान वेतनमान और समान िर पर होगी ।

पश् चातम, प्रत् येक अभ् यथी द्वारा प्राप् त मतों की संख् या और जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा करेगा । (5) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी इसके ीक पश् चातम पिाजधकाररयों के जनवााचन की कायावाजहयों को एक ररपोटा में अजभलेजखत करेगा िो सोसाइटी के अजभलेख का एक भाग होगा और सभी पर बाध् यकारी होगा । ररटर्नंग अजधकारी ऐसी ररपोटा की एक प्रजतजलजप के साथ मतिान की जववरणी की एक प्रजतजलजप प्राजधकरण को सौंपेगा। (6) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा जनवााचन के पररणाम की घोिणा प्राजधकरण के पूवा अनुमोिन से करेगा। (7) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा पररणामों की घोिण के पश् चातम, बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के मुख् य कायाकारी द्वारा जनवााचन प्रमाणपत्र तुरंत िारी दकए िाएंगे। 19-ण. मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान पर प्रवेि - (1) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, मतगणना के जलए जनयत स्ट् थान से जनम् नजलजखत के जसवाए, सभी ्‍ यजियों को बाहर रखेगा,— (क) ऐसे ्‍ यजियों को जिन्द् हें वह गणना में सहायता हेतु जनयुक्ट् त करे; (ख) ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि; (ग) जनवााचन से संबंजधत ड्यूटी पर लोक सेवक; और (घ) अभ् यथी । (2) ऐसे दकसी ्‍ यजि को िो जनवााचन में दकसी अभ् यथी के जलए अन्द् यथा काया कर रहा हो, उपजनयम (1) के खंड (क) के अधीन जनयुक्ट् त नहीं दकया िाएगा । (3) कोई ्‍ यजि िो मतगणना के िौरान किाचार करता है या ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के जवजधक जनिेिों का पालन करने में जवफल रहता है तो उसे मतगणना स्ट् थल से ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा या जनवााचन ड्यूटी पर तैनात दकसी पुजलस कमी द्वारा या इस जनजमत्त ररटर्नंग अजधकारी द्वारा प्राजधकृत दकए गए दकसी ्‍ यजि द्वारा हटा दिया िाएगा ।

जिकायतकताा ने ऑम् बुड्समसमैन के समि िाने से पूवा उसी जविय पर बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी को एक जलजखत अभ् यावेिन दिया हो, और: (i) ऐसा अभ् यावेिन रे कर दिया गया हो; (ii) अभ् यावेिन की प्रस्ट् तुत करने के पश् चातम एक महीने की अवजध के भीतर कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो; या (iii) जिकायतकताा ऐसे उत्तर से संतुष् ट न हो । (ख) जिकायतकताा द्वारा बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के उत्तर की प्राजप्त से एक महीने के भीतर जिकायत ििा की गई हो या, िब कोई उत्तर प्राप् त न हुआ हो, तो ऐसे अभ् यावेिन करने से िो महीने के भीतर; (ग) जिकायत या अपील की प्रकृजत अपमानिनक या तुच् छ या कष् टकारी न हो; और (घ) जिकायतकताा या अपीलकताा द्वारा जिकायत के जनपटान हेतु इन जनयमों में अपेजित पूरी सूचना प्रिान न की गई हो ।

ऐसे अभ् यथी जिसका नामांकन स्ट् वीकार दकया गया था, जनवााचन रे होने के पश् चातम ऐसे अभ् यथी की अभ् यर्थाता वापस लेने के नए नोरटस को स्ट् वीकार नहीं दकया िाएगा । 19ध. मतिान के जलए इलेक्ट् रॉजनक मतिान मिीनों तैयार करना - यदि प्राजधकरण मतिान के जलए इलेक्ट् रॉजनक मिीन का उपयोग करने का जनणाय लेता है तो वह इसकी प्रदक्रया जनिेजित करेगा िो िहां तक तकनीकी ूप प से यथािक्ट् य हो, इन जनयमों के अनुसार होगी । 19न. जनवााचन ्‍ यय – जनवााचन संबंधी सभी ्‍ यय जिसमें लेखन सामग्री, मुरण, डाक, फोटोकॉपी, फैक्ट् स, मत पेटी का दकराया, अजमट स्ट् याही, पुजलस सुरिा और अन्द् य ऐसे ्‍ यय की वस्ट् तुओं पर होने वाले ्‍ यय िो बहुराज् य सहकारी सोसाइटी के प्रजतजनजधयों या जनिेिकों के जनवााचन से संबंजधत है, िैसे मतिाता सूची की तैयारी, यात्रा और अन्द्य भत्ते, और ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, सहायक ररटर्नंग अजधकारी, और अन्द्य मतिान कर्मायों को िेय पाररश्रजमक का वहन सोसाइटी द्वारा दकया िाएगा और प्राजधकरण के जनिेि पर प्राजधकरण को भुगतान दकया िाएगा । 19प. जनवााचन ्‍ यय का लेखा - (1) जनवााचन का प्रत् येक अभ् यथी जनवााचन कराने के आिेि की तारीख से उसके पररणाम की घोिणा की तारीख, िोनों तारीख सजम्मजलत, तक जनवााचन से संबंजधत उसके द्वारा या उसके प्राजधकृत ्‍ यजि द्वारा दकए गए सभी ्‍ ययों का एक पृथक और सही लेखा पररणाम की घोिणा की तारीख से तीस दिनों की अवजध तक रखेगा । (2) इन लेखों में ऐसी जवजिजियां सजम्मजलत होंगी िो जनयम 19ब में जनर्िाष् ट जववरणों के अजतररक्ट् त समय-समय पर जवजनर्िाष् ट दकए िाएंगे । (3) उक्ट् त ्‍ यय की कुल रकम, प्राजधकरण द्वारा समय-समय पर जवजनर्िाष् ट की गई कुल रकम से अजधक नहीं होगी । (4) जनवााचन लड़ने वाला प्रत् येक अभ् यथी ररटर्नंग अजधकारी के पास अपने जनवााचन ्‍ यय के लेखा को प्राजधकरण द्वारा समय-समय पर जनर्िाष् ट रीजत और समय पर प्रस्ट् तुत करेगा ।

य सहकारी सोसाइटी का मुख् य कायाकारी ऐसी ररजियों की सूचना, इसके उद्भुत होने के एक सप् ताह के भीतर प्राजधकरण को संसूजचत करेगा, िो अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार ररजियों को भरने की कारावाई करेगा । (2) अजधजनयम की धारा 45ञ के उपबंधों के अनुसार वैकजल्पक ररजियों में जनयुक्ट् त कोई ्‍ यजि अजधिेि अवजध तक ही बोडा का सिस्ट् य रहेगा, िब तक वह बोडा के सिस्ट् य जिसके स्ट् थान पर जनयुक्ट् त हुआ है, रहेगा । 19य. मतिान की गोपनीयता का अनुरिण - प्रत् येक अजधकारी, जलजपक, अजभकताा या अन्द् य ्‍ यजि िो दकसी जनवााचन में अजभलेखन या मतगणना से िुड़ा काया जनष् पािन कर रहा है, मतगणना की गोपनीयता अनुरजित करेगा और अनुरिण करने में मिि करेगा और दकसी अन्द् य ्‍ यजि को (जसवाए कुछ प्रयोिनों के जलए दकसी जवजध द्वारा या उसके अधीन प्राजधकृत) ऐसी गोपनीयता का उल् लंघन करने के जलए मतिान से संबंजधत कोई सूचना संप्रेजित नहीं करेगा ।” 5. मूल जनयमों में, जनयम 20 के स्ट् थान पर जनम् नजलजखत जनयम रखे िाएंगे, अथाातम: -
